- **In the original F77?** No. ACFPFT is the convergence tolerance of SHAPE's iteration for r₀³, and its cube root the tolerance on r₀; nothing averages ([shape.f:44](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/shape.f#L44), [:95](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/shape.f#L95), [:112-113](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/shape.f#L112-L113), its default [parmin.f:434](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L434)):
  ```fortran
              IF(DABS(DELR03/R03).LE.ACFPFT)GOTO 20
           ACC = ACFPFT**CC13
  C  CORRECT ETA2 HERE IF DR/R0 > CUBE ROOT OF ACFPFT
              IF(DABS(ERR)/R0(I).LE.ACC) GOTO 70
  ```
  The description and the name came with [ae73704f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ae73704f) (2026-08-22), the first inlist format.
- **Now:** the registry row `acfpft`, [controls_registry.tsv:125](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L125) ("Averaging weight in the fp/ft update"), repeated by the generated `controls_registry.md`; the copy, [rotation_settings_setup.f90:90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/setup/rotation_settings_setup.f90#L90), into the field documented at [rotation_configuration.f90:48-54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/rotation/rotation_configuration.f90#L48-L54) and used by `rotating_shape.f90` ([:208-209](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/rotation/shape/rotating_shape.f90#L208-L209), [:267](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/rotation/shape/rotating_shape.f90#L267)).
- **What is wrong:** a newcomer reading the registry or the inlist name would take the control for a weight between 0 and 1; it is a relative tolerance (default 1e-36). `docs/source/namelist_physics.md` and the deck comments describe it correctly. `docs/GLOSSARY.md`'s trap 24 records the mismatch but cites `rotation/shape/shape.f90`, which does not exist (the file is `rotating_shape.f90`).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a control's name and description say what it does (M52's rule).
- **What we did:** the control's description, the comment above its declaration in `io/controls_buffer.f90` (so `physics.defaults` and `controls_registry.md`), reads "The rotating star's shape: the relative tolerance on r0^3 of the equipotential radius iteration (its cube root that on r0 and eta2); not a weight", and its two iteration limits (`fpft_iter1`, `fpft_iter2`) say which loop each bounds. Open: a readable inlist name with the old one as an alias; the alias would shadow the code name, which then needs the rename too, left for the renames.

- **Status:** open. The net review's item. Latent: it needs log T exactly equal to a cutoff.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, each comparison: KEMCOM's `.LT.`, MIX's `.LE.` and ENGEB's helium gate ([kemcom.f:74](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/kemcom.f#L74), [mix.f:141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mix.f#L141), [:209](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mix.f#L209), [engeb.f:811](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L811)):
  ```fortran
        IF(HT(IBEGIN).LT.TCUT(1))THEN                          ! kemcom.f
              IF(HT(J).LE.TCUT(1)) GOTO 45                     ! mix.f
        IF(TL.LT.TCUT(4)) GO TO 100                            ! engeb.f
  ```
  The comment came with [3fee9d4b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3fee9d4b) (2026-10-10).
- **Now:** [burn_step.f90:507](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L507) (`<`) against [:583](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L583), [:617](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L617) and [:667](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L667) (`<=`); the helium gate, [network.f90:296-297](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/network.f90#L296-L297) (`>=`), against [net_configuration.f90:36-37](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/net_configuration.f90#L36-L37) ("at or below which ... (4) helium burning is off").
- **What is wrong:** a mixed region whose innermost shell sits exactly at cutoff(1) skips the homogenize-only branch (`<`) and goes through `burn_implicitly` with the zero rates the other loops (`<=`) left it; helium burns at exactly cutoff(4), as network.f90's own comments say, while net_configuration says it is off there.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one rule for "below the cutoff", and a comment that says it.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `<=` at burn_step.f90:507, and net_configuration's comment for (4) corrected to the code's "below". Results change only at exact equality (no deck has been seen there).

### M119. test_eos's "OPAL 2006's first derivatives" check tests the OPAL 2001 table

- **Status:** fixed in [94e65af5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/94e65af5) (2026-11-10). Test only. The eos review's item. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No; the check came with [da05c29f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/da05c29f) (2026-10-29, round 2), already after the 2001 block.
- **Now:** `check_derivatives`, [test_eos.f90:463-493](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L463-L493): the 2006 points at [:479-480](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L479-L480), then OPAL 1995's and 2001's ([:481-484](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L481-L484)), then the check ([:485-486](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L485-L486)); `eos/README.md` §6 repeats its label.
- **What is wrong:** `derivative_points` resets `worst_first` for each configuration, so the check labelled OPAL 2006's judges the 2001 table's. 2001 and 2006 share the OPAL code, which is why the commit's mutation of OPAL's d ln ρ/d ln T could not show it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a check tests what its label says; the production configuration is OPAL 2006's.
- **What we did:** recorded at first, then fixed with the derivative check's rework for CI (its relative differences, round-off where the derivatives are analytic, are judged and no longer printed): the check follows the 2006 block, where the worst first derivative is 1.06e-3, and the 2001 and 1995 tables have their own, to 3e-3 and 1e-2 (1.0e-3 and 2.6e-3 now). A 5% mutation of OPAL's d ln ρ/d ln T fails all three; one applied to the 1995 table alone fails its check alone.

### M120. test_controls dumps two fields the read does not set and misses six it does

- **Status:** fixed in [3a44ae33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3a44ae33) and [58f6648f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/58f6648f) (2026-10-31, round 3). Test only. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. `test_controls` came with [89b04418](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/89b04418) (2026-10-11); [498cb8c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/498cb8c7) (2026-10-29) moved the envelope Z out of the read and kept its dump line; the pristine test's exclusion pattern came with [6085de4c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6085de4c) and went dead at [88b19e32](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/88b19e32) (both 2026-10-29), which moved `npenv` to the buffer.
- **Now:** the star fields of the dump, [test_controls.f90:69-81](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/test/test_controls.f90#L69-L81); the pinned zeros, [pristine.txt:1927-1928](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/test/expected_controls/pristine.txt#L1927-L1928); the scales `map_user_inputs` sets, [user_inputs.f90:116-124](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/user_inputs.f90#L116-L124), [:150-151](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/user_inputs.f90#L150-L151), [:162-186](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/user_inputs.f90#L162-L186); the pristine test, [test_controls.py:152-176](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/test_controls.py#L152-L176).
- **What is wrong:** the dump writes `envelope_hydrogen_fraction` (never set by the read: 0 in every dump since the test began) and `envelope_metal_fraction` (0 since 498cb8c7), and leaves out the six scales the read does set: `s_prime_scale`, `s_double_prime_scale`, `be7p_s_prime_scale`, `be7p_s_double_prime_scale`, `n15_pa_scale` and `n15_pg_scale`, which vary with the deck (529 decks, `sample_cases` included, set `use_new_nuclear_rates`). So `io/README.md` §4's "Any change to the read shows up here" is false for them. The pristine test compares only the `ctrl%` and `job%` keys, none of the 79 buffer-only members (`buffer%`), and its exclusion of `ctrl%npenv` matches no key now (`buffer%envelope_print_points`).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the dump is the read's whole output, so a change to the read cannot pass unseen.
- **What we did:** the six derivative and branch scales are derived controls in `star%physics` now, so they are dumped (`physics%...`); the dump writes every run copy (`star%<copy>`, 33 lines, each equal to its control in every deck) and not the two envelope fractions; the pristine test compares the buffer-only members too, leaving out the members the read derives by their registry status, and its dead `npenv` exclusion is gone.

### M121. reaction_rates' Sources give q7 with −ln S₀, where the fits use +ln S₀

- **Status:** open (doc). The net review's item, recomputed for all seven rows.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, ENGEB's comment ([engeb.f:252-253](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L252-L253), [:242](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L242), [:246](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L246); the same in rates.f):
  ```fortran
  C  TAU = Q6*(T SUB 9 TO THE (-1/3) POWER ).
  C NOTE THAT Q6 IS NEGATIVE.
  C  Q7 = 70.62860 + ((LN(Z0*Z1/A))/3) -LN(A0*A1) - LN(S SUB 0)
  C       -LN(1 + DELTA_01)
  ```
  The round-1 rewrite that resolved the Sources' contradictions ([ee5c6122](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ee5c6122), 2026-10-29) kept it; the retired F77 text it left (`net/retired/f77_rate_comments.txt`) lists two known slips, not this one.
- **Now:** [reaction_rates.f90:533-536](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L533-L536), against the law's own docstring ([:296-299](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L296-L299)); `net/README.md` §5's recipe for a new S-factor reaction sends the reader to these Sources for its `fit`.
- **What is wrong:** with +ln S₀ the formula gives every row's q7 to four decimals (pp 20.8964, ³He+³He 76.6003, ³He+⁴He 67.8036, p+¹²C 69.1300, p+¹³C 70.3809, p+¹⁴N 69.8517, p+¹⁶O 70.8012); with −ln S₀ pp would be 119.4028. The same sentence also says both "q6 = −τ(T9 = 1)" (Neutrino Astrophysics' τ, positive) and "τ = q6 T9^(−1/3)" (the code's, negative). A newcomer following the recipe would compute a q7 off by 2 ln S₀.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the formula in the Sources reproduces the table it documents.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: "+ ln S₀", and one convention for τ (the code's, the docstring's). Comments only.

### M122. opal_vintage_conflict is produced by nothing

- **Status:** fixed (doc) in [620c95c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/620c95c7) and [72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos). The eos review's item. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The F77's policy is the one the code follows, the newest vintage wins ([parmin.f:823-830](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L823-L830)):
  ```fortran
  C  Disable Older OPAL EOS's if a newer one is specified
        IF (LOPALE06) THEN
            LOPALE01 = .FALSE.
            LOPALE = .FALSE.
        ENDIF
  ```
  The error came with [3dafbbd8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3dafbbd8) (2026-10-29), unreachable from a deck already, and [12faddeb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/12faddeb) (2026-10-29) removed the builder's branch that could produce it.
- **Now:** the value and its stale comment, [eos_configuration.f90:16-20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/eos_configuration.f90#L16-L20); `eos_init`'s check, [eos_lib.f90:92-94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/eos_lib.f90#L92-L94), [:102-108](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/eos_lib.f90#L102-L108); `derive_controls`, [derived_controls.f90:98-115](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/derived_controls.f90#L98-L115), which warns and selects the newest; `eos/README.md` §4.
- **What is wrong:** the README and the comments describe a "two vintages" error that no deck can reach: `derive_controls` resolves the conflict before the settings are built, and the builder copies one vintage. Only `test_eos`'s settings check, which passes the value directly, sees it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the documentation describes the policy that runs, newest wins with a warning.
- **What we did:** the value stays, as `eos_init`'s range check; its comment (620c95c7) and README §3 (72b483a0) say that `derive_controls` lets the newest vintage win, so that no deck reaches the error. Comments and docs only.

### M123. adopt_table_result and blend_table_result drop the ionization fractions a new source fills

- **Status:** fixed (doc) in [72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos). The eos review's item, with a caution on the fix (below). Latent: OPAL, the only table source, fills none. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. OEQOS returned no ionization fractions ([eqstat2.f:274-275](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L274-L275)):
  ```fortran
           CALL OEQOS(TL,T,PL,P,D10o,Doo,X,Z,BETAo,BETAIo,
       1   BETA14o,RMUo,AMUo,EMUo,QDTo,QDPo,QCPo,DELAo,*998)
  ```
  The helpers came with [2c03cfba](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2c03cfba) and the README's recipe with [9ce8e797](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9ce8e797) (both 2026-10-29).
- **Now:** [blended_eos.f90:461-504](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L461-L504); `eos_result`, [eos_results.f90:26-56](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L26-L56); `eos/README.md` §7, the source recipe.
- **What is wrong:** the recipe tells a new source to fill the ionization fractions and to hand its result to these two helpers, which copy ρ, β, the mean weights and the first derivatives but not `ion_fraction` (nor η), so a new source's fractions are dropped without a word.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the recipe and the helpers agree.
- **What we did:** README §6's source recipe, rewritten for the table-source descriptor, says which fields `adopt_table_result` and `blend_table_result` carry (with M148's correction); the helpers are unchanged. Copying `ion_fraction` unconditionally would zero the Yale and SCV fractions on every OPAL point (OPAL's `table_r` holds zeros), which kap reads: that would change results.

### M124. Three math statements: pow "matches x**y exactly", "within a few ulp of y ln x", and CI runs test_math

- **Status:** open (doc). The math review's items, checked on a scratch build with crmath. Round 3: the third part, CI, holds once CI's first run on `yrec-next` passes (M125, fixed locally); the two comment parts stay open.
- **In the original F77?** No; `math_lib` is 2026. The pow comment came with [3cfc5cb8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3cfc5cb8) (2026-08-30) and was reworded by [023d5080](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/023d5080), which also wrote the README's table; the test's label came with [c2638e4b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c2638e4b); the README's CI sentence with [42048e86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/42048e86) (all 2026-10-29).
- **Now:** [math_lib.f90:106-108](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/math/math_lib.f90#L106-L108), inside the crmath branch; the label at [test_math.f90:88](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/math/test/test_math.f90#L88), with the test's tolerance at [:83-84](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/math/test/test_math.f90#L83-L84); `math/README.md` §2's table and §5's CI sentence.
- **What is wrong:**
  - The comment says `pow_r(x, real(y, dp))` "matches x**y exactly"; under crmath, where it sits, it does not (826 of 1000 x differ at y = 0.6666667; at x = 3.7 by 1.9e-16 relative). It is true of the intrinsic branch.
  - "Within a few ulp of y ln x": the composition exp(y ln x) loses about |y ln x| ulp (26 ulp at |y ln x| = 28, up to about 900 near 300), as the test's own tolerance, a few ulp times max(1, |y ln x|), allows. The wording reads as a few ulp.
  - The README says CI builds `test_math` and runs `test_math.py`; the workflow lists both, but as configured its job fails at an earlier step and no push to `yrec-next` starts it (M125).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a comment states what its branch does; an error bound says how it scales.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: move the "exactly" to the intrinsic branch, say "within a few ulp times |y ln x|", and make the CI sentence true (M125) or conditional. Comments and docs only.

### M126. A second core extension in one run starts from the first one's log-mass shift, not the deck's factor

- **Status:** open. Found by the controls split (2026-10-30), which made the factor's working copy a star member, `core_mass_reduction`; recorded on the member, not fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. STARIN overwrites the factor with the shift it computes: `MCORE = INT(DLOG10(FCORE)/HPTTOL(2))+1` and `FCORE = DBLE(MCORE)*HPTTOL(2)` ([starin.f:375-376](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L375-L376)), with FCORE in /CORE/; MHP 9/14 made the extension run on every card that reads the starting model (LFIRST(NK)).
- **Now:** [starting_model.f90:509-515](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/9dabfccf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L509-L515): `s%num_core_points_added = int(log10(s%core_mass_reduction)/ ...)+1`, then `s%core_mass_reduction = dble(s%num_core_points_added)* ...`.
- **What is wrong:** the extension runs on every card that reads its model from file, so a second such card in one run (every solar-calibration cycle, for one) takes the first card's log10 mass shift N dlog m as if it were the reduction factor: log10 of a number below 1 gives N = 0 or 1 points, whatever the deck asked for.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each extension takes the deck's `core_mass_reduction_factor`; the shift is a result, not a new factor.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. 199 shipped decks set `extend_core_inward`; which of them read the starting model on more than one card was not checked, and nothing was measured. Proposed fix: keep the factor and compute the shift into a local; results change for the decks it reaches, so its own measured commit.

## 10. Found in the fourth evaluation (2026-10-31)

On 2026-10-31 the five reviews of sections 7-9 were repeated a fourth time, at [e8c847ba](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e8c847ba), after the controls split, and scored out of 10 (`audit/module-evaluation-4-2026-10-31/SUMMARY.md`). They did not re-report section 9's open items; each listed the new defects it found beside its style and structure suggestions. These items are those defects. Each entry records what is wrong, the proposed fix and whether it would change results. Round 3 (2026-10-31/11-01, section 11) fixed M130, M138, M140, M143, M149-M155 and M163-M165; their entries say how, with M130's measurement. The others are open.

- M127-M130 are the items whose fix would change results: the Li6 rate scale first, which reaches 1,175 shipped decks; then SCV's H⁺ fraction (through the conductive opacity), the two 1/μ_ion rules under diffusion of Z (output only) and FGONG's global values (no shipped deck writes FGONG). M131-M140 are latent defects and error paths, M141-M145 tests and checkers that check less than they say, and M146-M165 documentation a newcomer would act on: the recipes first (M146-M150), then descriptions and comments.
- **How they were checked.** Every item was read again in the code at d6a66ffe (the code of e8c847ba) and against the F77 import before its entry was written. The numbers were recomputed: M127's S(0) values from the fits' prefactors (the review's Li6 value was too small by the reduced mass), M128's overstatement from the shipped `h_tab_i.dat`, M129's difference from the default mixture, and every deck count by a scan of the repository's decks. The cases of M131, M133-M135, M140-M143, M145, M148-M150 and M157 were run on scratch copies (of net/, numerics/, math/ and eos/ modules, of the checkers and generators, of a crmath build, and of src/). No deck was run, so the drifts a fix would cause are not measured. Where the check corrected a review (a line, a number, a claim, where it reaches), the entry gives the corrected account and says so.
- **Left out.** These statements the reviews called false hold on a reading of the code: net/README:157's "a new species or reaction changes the pins, not the program" (a new reaction still reaches the pinned dX/dt), numerics/README §3's sentence on the searches, the run copy `num_rotation_structure_passes` (the run does change it, as its comment says), the "Private to one module" banner (M163), setup/README's coverage figure (M164) and four of io's stale phrases (M165). Also left out, by this section's rule: the self-check gaps of `network_checks` (true, but no header or recipe claims those checks), mutate_numerics.py's dead strings (every mutation still applies), and the reviews' style and structure points (setup's install module, the builders' purity, `max_runs`, io's imports through legacy_controls and `interpret_kind_cards`' unused argument, net_lib's two dead exports, the history comments).
- Current-code links point at [d6a66ffe](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/d6a66ffe/src). For an item round 3 fixed, they show the code before the fix; its "What we did" says where the fix is.

### M127. The Li/Be overrides scale each fit against a reference that is not its S(0), so the shipped decks burn Li6 at 0.57 times the rate they ask for

- **Status:** open. The net review's item, recomputed (below): the review's S(0) of 2689 keV b for the Li6 fit is too small by the reduced mass. Results change when fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. G. Somers' 2014 overrides divide each cross section by a reference from an older compilation, in PARMIN, and LIRATE88 multiplies the Caughlan & Fowler 1988 rates by the quotient ([parmin.f:800-808](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L800-L808), [:818-820](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L818-L820), [lirate88.f:52-55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/lirate88.f#L52-L55), [:86-91](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/lirate88.f#L86-L91)):
  ```fortran
  C          DEFAULT LI6 = 5.5 MeV b FROM FOWLER ET AL. 1967           ! parmin.f
            SLI6 = XSLI6/5.5D3
           FLI6=3.73D10/T923*EXP(-8.413D0/T913-(T9/5.50D0)**2)*       ! lirate88.f
           FLI6=SLI6*FLI6
  ```
  The references got their names (`li6_reference_xs`, ...) with [e22cf809](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e22cf809), and net/README's "one edit" sentence came with [90d39ba2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90d39ba2) (both 2026-10-29, round 2).
- **Now:** the references, [legacy_controls.f90:222-228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L222-L228); `derive_rate_scales`, [derived_controls.f90:74-85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/derived_controls.f90#L74-L85); the fits and their scales, `compute_li_be_rates`, [light_elements.f90:321-368](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/light_elements.f90#L321-L368) (Li6 at [:339-342](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/light_elements.f90#L339-L342), Li7 at [:347-348](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/light_elements.f90#L347-L348), Be9 at [:350-360](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/light_elements.f90#L350-L360), the scales at [:362-366](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/light_elements.f90#L362-L366)); the registry rows, [controls_registry.tsv:291-300](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L291-L300); net/README §3's "Scales", [README.md:141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/README.md#L141).
- **What is wrong:** each `*_rate_value` (keV b) becomes the scale value/reference on a Caughlan & Fowler 1988 fit, which reproduces the requested cross section only if the reference is that fit's S(0). For a non-resonant term P T9^(−2/3) exp(−a T9^(−1/3)) (1 + ...), the Gamow-peak integral gives P = (2/3) N_A (8/μ)^(1/2) (a/(k · 10⁹ K))^(1/2) S(0), that is 7.83e6 (Z0Z1/Â)^(1/3) S(0) with S in keV b (the constant of M91). The same formula gives pp's S(0) as 4.07e-22 keV b from its 4.01e-15 (net's `s0_kevb`, [network.f90:199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L199)), each fit's τ coefficient from 4.2487 (Z0²Z1²Â)^(1/3) (8.415, 8.473 and 10.361 against the fits' 8.413, 8.472 and 10.359), and the fits' T9^(1/3) coefficients as 5/(12a) (0.050 and 0.040). With the atomic masses:
  - Li6(p,α): 3.73e10 gives S(0) = 3144 keV b (3133 with integer masses), against the reference 5500 ("Fowler et al. 1967"), a factor 0.572. The older fit the F77 kept in a comment has the same prefactor, so 5500 is neither fit's.
  - Li7(p,α): as T9 → 0 the two terms combine to 1.096e9 − 4.830e8 = 6.13e8, S(0) = 52.0 keV b, the reference (Rolfs & Kavanagh 1986).
  - Be9(p,γ): 1.33e7 gives 1.035 keV b, against 1.1 (a factor 0.941).
  - Be9(p,d) and Be9(p,α): their shared non-resonant 2.11e11 gives 16.4 MeV b, against 15 (a factor 1.095).

  1,176 decks set all five overrides, to 3100, 52, 1.2, 15000 and 21000 keV b ("Cross-section for p+6Li (KeV barns)", for example [Test_3Msolar_..._RGp2diffrotI0.inlist:153-162](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/testsuite/Test_3Msolar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10_RGp2diffrotI0.inlist#L153-L162)): 1,159 inlists in examples/, grid/, sample_cases/, startmodels/ and testsuite/, and the 17 legacy `.nml2` decks in examples/. All but one also set `use_extended_composition`, without which the light elements are not followed. Those 1,175 burn Li6 with S(0) = 3100/5500 × 3144 = 1772 keV b, 0.572 of the 3100 they ask for; Be9 by (p,d) and (p,α) at 1.095 of their requests and by (p,γ) at 0.941; Li7 as asked. The review's 2689 keV b is 3137 × 6/7: its formula divides once more by Â, which is also where its factors for Li7 (0.87) and Be9(p,γ) (0.85) come from, and its counts (1160 inlists and 18 legacy decks; the summary's 1,036) are recounted above. The references sit in io/, away from the fits they normalize, so net/README §3's "Each is defined once, so changing a fit's normalization and its reference is one edit" does not hold for them, and §1.2 lists `legacy_controls` only for `sstandard`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** `li6_rate_value = 3100` gives the Li6 rate whose S(0) is 3100 keV b: a scale is relative to the S(0) of the fit it multiplies, as `map_user_inputs` scales the S-factor inputs against `reference_s0`.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: each fit's S(0) beside it in light_elements (3144, 52.0, 1.035, 16430 and 16430 keV b, or computed from its prefactor), exported through net_lib as `reference_s0` is, and `derive_rate_scales` scales against those (the inputs' defaults with them); a test_net check that each reference is its fit's S(0). Results change for the 1,175 decks: Li6 burns 1.75 times faster (a scale of 0.986 for 0.564), Be9 by (p,d) and (p,α) 0.913 times as fast and by (p,γ) 1.06 times; surface Li6 and Be9 move, Li7 does not. Not measured: its own measured commit, on the pre-main-sequence and solar decks.

### M128. SCV's H⁺ fraction counts each H₂ molecule as one hydrogen nucleus

- **Status:** open. The eos review's item, recomputed from the shipped table and corrected on where it reaches (below). Results change when fixed, through the conductive opacity (not measured).
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQSCVE and EQSCVG divide H⁺ by the hydrogen particles, while SETSCV counts the hydrogen nuclei with H₂ twice ([eqscve.f:436-446](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscve.f#L436-L446), [eqscvg.f:309](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscvg.f#L309), [setscv.f:44-45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setscv.f#L44-L45)):
  ```fortran
        XTF_H_e = .5D0*(1D0 - XTF_H2 - XTF_H1)                        ! eqscve.f
        XTF_HP = XTF_H_e
        XHP = XTF_HP / (XTF_H2 + XTF_H1 + XTF_HP)
              HNUM = 2.0D0*YM1*DMIX/CMH/                              ! setscv.f
       *             (1.0D0+3.0D0*TABLEX(I,J,2)+TABLEX(I,J,3))
  ```
- **Now:** `scv_ionization_fractions`, [scv_eos.f90:617-652](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L617-L652) (the H⁺ fraction at [:649](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L649)), called by both SCV lookups ([:285](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L285), [:534](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L534)); the envelope table's build, [:715-717](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L715-L717); `gas_eos`, which takes SCV's fractions where its table covers the point ([blended_eos.f90:247-253](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L247-L253)), the Saha ramp, which blends them toward the fully ionized gas's ([:427](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L427)), and `adopt_table_result`, which leaves them ([:461-476](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L461-L476), M123).
- **What is wrong:** columns 2 and 3 of the H table are the fractions of all particles (H₂, H, H⁺ and electrons) that are H₂ and H, as the routine's comment ([:624-625](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L624-L625)) and the build take them, and charge balance gives x_H⁺ = x_e = (1 − x_H₂ − x_H)/2 ([:643-644](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L643-L644)). The hydrogen nuclei number 2x_H₂ + x_H + x_H⁺, so the fraction of them that is ionized, which the comment at [:647-648](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L647-L648) says the routine returns, is (1 − x_H₂ − x_H)/(1 + 3x_H₂ + x_H); the code divides by x_H₂ + x_H + x_H⁺ and gets (1 − x_H₂ − x_H)/(1 + x_H₂ + x_H), too high by the factor 1 + 2x_H₂/(1 + x_H₂ + x_H), which tends to 2 where the gas is molecular. The helium fractions are right (no molecules).
  - Recomputed at the 3720 nodes of the shipped [h_tab_i.dat](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/input/eos/scv/h_tab_i.dat): among those with an H⁺ fraction above 1e-4 and log P_gas ≤ 10, the largest overstatement is 32.7%, at log T 4.02, log P 10 (3.81e-4 against 2.87e-4), as the review says; at higher pressure, where pressure ionization meets H₂, it is 96% at log T 3.62, log P 12.0 (an H⁺ fraction of 1.25%) and 98% at log P 11.8.
  - Where it reaches: `ion_fraction(1)` weights hydrogen in kap's conductive opacity ([conductive_opacity.f90:138](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L138)), which all 1,159 inlists use (`use_conductive_opacity`), at every `kap_get` after an EOS call ([shell_physics.f90:111-113](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/shell_physics.f90#L111-L113), [shell_equations.f90:185-187](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/structure/shell_equations.f90#L185-L187), [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:456-457](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L456-L457)). Since OPAL's adopt step leaves the fractions, SCV's value stands wherever SCV covers a zone below the Saha ramp, inside the OPAL table or not. The review's "envelope and atmosphere ionization outputs" are records the envelope integration fills and nothing writes out ([envelope_points.f90:41-42](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/envelope_points.f90#L41-L42), [:61-62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/envelope_points.f90#L61-L62)).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the fraction of the hydrogen nuclei that are ionized has the nuclei, 2x_H₂ + x_H + x_H⁺, in its denominator, as the table's build counts them.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: 2x_H₂ in the denominator at [:649](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L649), after confirming that the tables' X_H₂ and X_H are per particle (Saumon, Chabrier & Van Horn 1995), as the F77's comment and the build take them. Results change for the decks with zones where SCV covers H₂ and H⁺ together, cool dense envelopes of the low-mass decks, through the conductive opacity's weight; which zones, and by how much, not measured.

### M129. With diffusion of Z, OPAL's and MHD's 1/μ_ion count a zone's extra metals as carbon, while the Yale and SCV paths scale the mixture

- **Status:** open. The eos review's item, recomputed and corrected (below: the step is a drift across OPAL's edge ramp, and the test the review proposes would not see it). Results change when fixed: 1/μ_ion and 1/μ_e in the 355 shipped decks that run with diffusion of Z, in the output (counted on 2026-11-02 from what the read gives each deck; the count of 186 inlists by deck text missed the 169 decks that `diffuse_lithium` puts on it, M181).
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQSTAT2 alone branches on `LDIFZ` and scales every metal; inside an OPAL table it then takes OEQOS06's `AMU`, which MU computes with the excess metals as carbon whatever `LDIFZ` is, and MEQOS calls MU the same way ([eqstat2.f:62-81](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L62-L81), [:384](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L384), [mu.f:22-37](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mu.f#L22-L37), [oeqos06.f:97](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/oeqos06.f#L97), [meqos.f:62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/meqos.f#L62)):
  ```fortran
        IF(LDIFZ)THEN                                                  ! eqstat2.f
           RAT = Z/ZENV
  ...
              AMU=AMUo
  C ASSUME EXCESS Z(METALS) IS IN THE FORM OF CARBON(12)               ! mu.f
           AMU = AMUENV + DFX1 + DFX4 + DFX12
  ```
- **Now:** `compute_mean_weights`, [eos_mixture.f90:112-136](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_mixture.f90#L112-L136), through `ion_mean_weight_excess` ([:82-103](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_mixture.f90#L82-L103), the carbon at [:96-101](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_mixture.f90#L96-L101)), called by `compute_opal_eos` ([opal_eos.f90:158-160](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L158-L160)) and `compute_mhd_eos` ([mhd_eos.f90:105-107](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L105-L107)); `zone_mixture`'s diffusion branch, [blended_eos.f90:329-360](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L329-L360), which gives the Yale and SCV paths their 1/μ_ion; `adopt_table_result` and `blend_table_result`, which copy or blend OPAL's into the zone's result ([:470-471](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L470-L471), [:492-495](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L492-L495)).
- **What is wrong:** `compute_mean_weights` ignores `use_diffusion_z`. With it, a zone whose Z differs from the envelope's by ΔZ gets, on the Yale and SCV paths, 1/μ_ion = Σ_env + ΔZ⟨1/A⟩ + (the H and He terms), with Σ_env the envelope's Σ X_i/A_i and every metal scaled with Z/Z_env, but where OPAL (or MHD) gives the result Σ_env + ΔZ × 0.08322 + (the same H and He terms), the excess as carbon. The difference is ΔZ(0.08322 − ⟨1/A⟩). Recomputed from the default mixture seed (X = 0.70, Z_env = 0.016492): ⟨1/A⟩ of its metals is 0.05978, so at Z = 1.1 Z_env OPAL's 1/μ_ion is 0.7659619 and the Yale/SCV value 0.7659232, 3.866e-5 apart; the review's scratch driver gives the same two values at log T 5, log P 12.80 (inside the OPAL 2006 table) and 13.05 (beyond it). It is not a jump: across the table's edge ramp, one table cell wide, `blend_table_result` blends the two linearly, so at fixed composition 1/μ_ion drifts by that much from one side to the other. R/μ is βP/(ρT) on both sides, so 1/μ_e, backed out of it, carries the difference with the opposite sign. Where it reaches:
  - the 355 shipped decks that run with `use_diffusion_z` (353 inlists and 2 legacy pairs, from what the read gives each deck), all on OPAL 2006 and SCV: the 186 inlists that set it (146 in sample_cases/; 27 of `run_from_zahb_to_tahb`, 12 testsuite decks and one of `run_config_matrix`), and 169 decks that set it off with `diffuse_lithium` on, which turns it on (M181: 84 of `run_from_seed_to_start`, 78 of `run_from_start_to_dbl`, the five rotating configuration-matrix decks and two settling solar pairs);
  - there the two mean weights feed only output: 1/μ_e goes to the pulse files and the optional profile column `mu_e_inv` (commented out in the default list) ([structure_equations.f90:322](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/structure/structure_equations.f90#L322), [stitched_model.f90:556](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L556), [:747](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L747), [profile_columns.list:68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/profile_columns.list#L68)); semiconvection reads only their sum, R/μ over R ([semiconvection.f90:188-189](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/convection/semiconvection.f90#L188-L189)), and the envelope's copy `qemu` is stored and never read.
  - README §2.1 gives the mixture rule as the zone's ([README.md:32](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L32)) and says OPAL's mean weights replace the result ([:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L43)), without saying that they follow the other rule.
  - `test_eos` cannot see it: `results_agree` ([test_eos.f90:1192-1220](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L1192-L1220)) compares R/μ and 1/μ_e but not 1/μ_ion, and every evaluation with diffusion of Z is either at the envelope's Z (the pinned `diffusion_z` configuration, [:335-336](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L335-L336); `diffusion_z_checks`, [:965-980](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L965-L980)) or with a metal-free envelope, where both paths take the excess rule ([:981-996](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L981-L996)).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a zone has one 1/μ_ion, whichever source gives its density, and it is the zone's composition's. Neither rule is that in general: in the helium-burning cores of the `run_from_zahb_to_tahb` decks Z grows by carbon and oxygen, which the scaling counts as envelope metals and the excess rule as carbon alone.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: one rule on every path. Either `compute_opal_eos` and `compute_mhd_eos` take the 1/μ_ion that `zone_mixture`'s rule gives (OPAL's step already holds it in r), as the review proposes; or every path takes 1/μ_ion from the zone's composition when `eos_get` is given it, as the Debye-Hückel record does (M66). With it, a check that under diffusion of Z, at a Z other than the envelope's, 1/μ_ion is the same inside the OPAL table and beyond it. (The review's test, `results_agree` comparing 1/μ_ion with one ramp run under diffusion of Z, would pass as now: the blend is continuous at both ends of the ramp, and the ramp check runs at the envelope's composition.) Results change for the 355 decks: with the first fix, 1/μ_ion and 1/μ_e by up to ΔZ × 0.023 in the output and their sum only by rounding; with the second, the Yale and SCV paths' densities too. Not measured.

### M130. FGONG's globals 4 to 6 are the current surface Z and X and a zero mixing length, where FGONG and MESA have the initial Z and X and α

- **Status:** fixed in [82bd89fc](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/82bd89fc) (2026-10-31, round 3). Results change for FGONG files only, in globals 4-6; no shipped deck writes one. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The F77 wrote no FGONG file. Its own pulsation model file (`LPULSE`, unit `IOPMOD`) carried the mixing length and the card's starting X and Z in its header, written by WRTMOD ([wrtmod.f:192-200](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmod.f#L192-L200); `XENV0` and `ZENV0` are the card's `XENV0A(NK)` and `ZENV0A(NK)`, [main.f:278-279](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L278-L279)):
  ```fortran
           WRITE (IOPMOD, 5001) MODEL,IDM,IPVER,QSMASS,
       1         TEFFL,BL,TEMPR, DAGE, CMIXL, XENV0, ZENV0
       *          ' MIXING LENGTH PARAMETER=', 0PF16.10,/,
       *          ' ZAMS (X,Z)=', 2F18.10)
  ```
  The FGONG writer came with [eb624a69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/eb624a69) (2026-08-22), ported from MESA's, with glob(4) and glob(5) the outermost shell's composition and glob(6) zero; `docs/ROADMAP.md` §6 has kept glob(6) as optional since ("fill if a consumer needs them").
- **Now:** `write_fgong_pulse`'s globals, [pulsation_output.f90:61-71](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L61-L71) (glob(4) and glob(5) at [:65-66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L65-L66), the comment at [:67-68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L67-L68)), taken from point `n`, the top of the atmosphere, whose composition is the surface shell's ([stitched_model.f90:807-808](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L807-L808)); called by `write_pulse` ([yrec_output.f90:265-267](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L265-L267)). The run's α, `s%mixing_length_alpha`, is in the history header beside the initial X and Z ([history_output.f90:336-340](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/history_output.f90#L336-L340)) and in the `.mod` ([model_files.f90:173](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/model_files.f90#L173)). `test_mesa_output.py` reads an FGONG file's globals 2 and 14 only ([test_mesa_output.py:195-199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/test_mesa_output.py#L195-L199)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - glob(6) is 0, with the comment "not tracked here", though the star holds α and the history and `.mod` files write it.
  - glob(4) and glob(5) are the surface Z and X at the model's age. The FGONG notes define glob(4) as Z, "heavy element abundance", and glob(5) as X₀, "initial hydrogen abundance" (MESA r26.04.1, adipls/adipack.c/notes/file-format.tex:122-123), and MESA writes `s%initial_z`, `1 - (s%initial_y + s%initial_z)` and `s%mixing_length_alpha` there (MESA r26.04.1, star/private/pulse_fgong.f90:171-176). The review recalled MESA as doing what YREC does; it does not. The two differ wherever settling or mixing has changed the surface: on the settling solar deck `Test_solar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10` (its committed baseline, `examples/run_standard_solar_model/standard/mesa/`), the surface at 4.49 Gyr (profile 9, zone 1) has X = 0.73637 and Z = 0.016816, against the initial 0.713208 and 0.017968 of its history header, so glob(5) is 3.2% high and glob(4) 6.4% low; its α is 1.822729, written as 0.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a code reading an FGONG file gets the model's initial composition and its mixing length, as from a MESA file, and the same values the history header gives.
- **What we did:** glob(4) = `card_initial_z(1)`, glob(5) = `card_initial_x(1)` and glob(6) = `mixing_length_alpha`: the run's initial Z and X, the first card's starting composition (the history header's `initial_z` and `initial_x`; in a calibration the first cycle's), and α, as MESA's `pulse_fgong` writes them. Decided (revisable): the first card's rather than the current card's, which is 0 on an evolve card whose deck leaves it unset (M172). Measured: `cm_base` writing FGONG every 2 models, glob(5) 0.719606 → 0.71962 and glob(6) 0 → 1.707575, glob(4) unchanged; the settling deck `Test_solar_GS_norot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10` (an FGONG at 3.5e7 yr), glob(4) 0.0187993 → 0.018804, glob(5) 0.708552 → 0.708483, glob(6) 0 → 1.852729; every other value identical. `test_mesa_output.py` checks the three against the history header, `test_io` against the star; four mutations caught.

### M131. burn_implicitly can return ierr 0 with all-NaN abundances when the NaN is only in the Newton right-hand side

- **Status:** open. The net review's item, confirmed on a scratch copy and corrected (below: which builds reach it). Latent: it needs a NaN in a solved species of a region's start-of-step composition, and the silent success then needs a build whose `max` drops the NaN.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. KEMCOM's convergence test could not see a NaN correction either: `.GE.` with a NaN is false, so the largest corrections BIGD and BIGB never take it and the system counts as converged, and SIMEQC took a NaN pivot without a test ([kemcom.f:313-327](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/kemcom.f#L313-L327), [simeqc.f:20-24](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/simeqc.f#L20-L24)):
  ```fortran
        IF(J1J.NE.0) CALL SIMEQC(A,8,7)                        ! kemcom.f
           IF(DABS(B(I)).GE.BIGD) BIGD = DABS(B(I))
        IF(BIGD.GE.ABSTOL.OR.BIGB.GE.RELTOL) THEN
        IF(DABS(BIGA).GE.DABS(A(IJ))) GO TO 30                 ! simeqc.f
        BIGA=A(IJ)
  ```
  So the F77 accepted a NaN on every build and wrote it into HCOMP (the test, transcribed, gives "converged" for seven NaN corrections at -O0 and -O3). [6846ee78](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6846ee78) (2026-10-10) wrote the test as `max(max_abs_change, abs(correction(i)))`, whose result for a NaN depends on the build; `simeqc`'s NaN-pivot test came with [def22898](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/def22898) and the mapping of every `simeqc` failure to `burn_singular_jacobian` with [360944cf](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/360944cf) (both 2026-10-29, round 2; M102): they catch a NaN in the Jacobian, not one in the right-hand side alone.
- **Now:** `burn_implicitly`, [network.f90:533-617](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L533-L617): its header's two codes ([:526-532](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L526-L532)), the residual ([:556-558](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L556-L558)), the solve and its one error ([:583-590](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L583-L590)), the convergence test ([:592-604](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L592-L604)); `simeqc`, which tests the pivot only ([linear_solvers.f90:182-186](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L182-L186), [:227-230](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L227-L230)); `burn_network_region`, which reports the two codes and writes `x` into the composition it is given ([burn_step.f90:522-540](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L522-L540), [:549-552](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L549-L552)): `s%xa` from `burn_network` ([:709-710](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L709-L710)), the rotation sub-step's composition from `mid_timestep_model` ([mid_timestep_model.f90:442-444](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/rotation/mid_timestep_model.f90#L442-L444)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - A NaN in a solved species of `x_start` (the region's start-of-step composition, `s%xa_start`, mass-averaged over a convection zone) enters the residual x − x_start − dt A dX/dt alone; the Jacobian, built from `x` and the rates, stays finite, so `simeqc` finds finite pivots, returns `numerics_ok`, and its back-substitution spreads the NaN over every correction. The convergence test then takes `max(max_abs_change, abs(NaN))`, and `max_rel_change` likewise (`x(i) < min_abundance` is false for a NaN `x(i)`). The standard does not define `max` of a NaN.
  - Confirmed on a scratch copy of net/, numerics/, math/ and state/ at d6a66ffe with an io_units stub and the review's drivers (`drive_nan.f90`, `drive_nan2.f90`: log ρ 2.2, log T 7.3, dt 3e13 s), rebuilt with the Makefile's GNU base flags, without crmath or HDF5 (gfortran 15.2, arm64 macOS). With a NaN in `x_start(He3)` or `x_start(C13)`: at -O0 and -O2 `ierr` is 0 and all eight abundances are NaN (O18 from the NaN abundances): `max` dropped the NaN and the test passed on the first iteration. At -O3, the flags of `make` and of every test program, `max` kept it, the next iteration's Jacobian held NaN and the pivot test gave `ierr` 2, M102's "singular" message, and the run stops. Under `make devel` and `make debug` (`-ffpe-trap=invalid`) it stops with a floating-point trap inside `burn_implicitly` (SIGILL here); the review counted the debug build among those that return 0. A NaN in a rate (`rv_frac_n15_pa` or `r_pc13`) gives `ierr` 2 at every level.
  - So on a gfortran build without traps below -O3 (`tools/coverage.py`'s -O0 --coverage build, or any -O2 build) and on any compiler whose `max` drops a NaN, `burn_network_region` writes the NaNs into `s%xa` (or the sub-step's composition) with `ierr` 0 and no message, against code style 7 ("never reports a success it did not have", [GUIDELINES.md:379-382](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/docs/GUIDELINES.md#L379-L382)) and against the header, which promises convergence only when every |correction| is below the tolerances. Where no off-diagonal entry is left, the residual itself is taken as the correction and `simeqc` is not called ([:583-590](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L583-L590)), so a NaN there passes the same way. `test_net` has no NaN case.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a non-finite correction is a failure, with a code of its own; whether the burn reports success must not depend on how the compiler evaluates `max`.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: before the convergence test, `burn_implicitly` returns a named code when `.not. all(ieee_is_finite(correction))`, the code M102 proposes for a non-finite Newton system (one code covers both), and `burn_network_region` reports it as such; a `test_net` check with a NaN in `x_start`. Byte-identical on the shipped decks (none reaches it); the release build's message for this case changes.

### M132. A derivative failure inside the envelope's bsstep ends the run as "solution diverged", exit 0; the same failure at the step's end exits 1

- **Status:** open. The numerics review's item (a caller of numerics), corrected (below) and checked against the F77. Error path: a run whose EOS or opacity fails inside the atmosphere or envelope integration exits 0 or 1 according to where in the step the failure falls; no committed output holds either bsstep message.
- **In the original F77?** No. QATM and QENV, BSSTEP's derivatives, had no status: an EOS or opacity failure inside them stopped the run where it happened (GETOPAC's `STOP`, for one), at a midpoint substep as at ENVINT's own call after the step, so one failure ended one way ([envint.f:563-565](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L563-L565), [:571-572](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L571-L572), [qenv.f:42-46](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/qenv.f#L42-L46), [getopac.f:141-144](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopac.f#L141-L144)):
  ```fortran
           CALL BSSTEP(Y,DYDX,NV,X0,H,EPS,YSCAL,HDID,HNEXT,QENV,        ! envint.f
           CALL QENV(X0,Y,DYDX,B,FPL,FTL,GL,LATMO,LDERIV,LOCOND,
           WRITE(ISHORT,*)'NO OPACITY TABLE CHOSEN',                    ! getopac.f
           STOP
  ```
  BSSTEP's one failure of its own, the vanishing step, was `ERROR IN BSSTEP` and `STOP` ([bsstep.f:51-53](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/bsstep.f#L51-L53), M57): the historical stop that `envelope_termination` keeps. The split came with [62346446](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/62346446) (2026-08-30), which gave the integrands an `ierr` and routed a failure inside bsstep "like a diverged step" (the termination code), while the kernel's own calls passed theirs up; [33f6ca61](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/33f6ca61) (2026-10-29, round 1) gave bsstep the optional `derivatives_ierr` for the code, which neither envelope call passes ("maps every other bsstep failure to numerics_termination as before", its message says).
- **Now:** `take_atmosphere_step` and `take_envelope_step`: the bsstep calls without `derivatives_ierr`, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:544-545](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L544-L545) and [:861-862](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L861-L862), every failure but bad input mapped to `envelope_termination` ([:547-558](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L547-L558), [:864-873](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L864-L873)), and the kernel's own derivative calls after an accepted step, which return their code ([:562-571](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L562-L571), [:879-888](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L879-L888)); `envelope_termination` and its comment, [:75-79](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L75-L79); the integrands' EOS and opacity returns, [envelope_integrands.f90:109-117](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integrands.f90#L109-L117) and [:224-232](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integrands.f90#L224-L232); bsstep's failure on the derivatives, [bulirsch_stoer.f90:133-137](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/bulirsch_stoer.f90#L133-L137), documented at [:74-76](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/bulirsch_stoer.f90#L74-L76); the exit, [main.f90:20-23](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/main.f90#L20-L23), and the C API's reading of a negative status, [yrec_capi.f90:19-23](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L19-L23).
- **What is wrong:**
  - An EOS or opacity failure at any of mmid's substep points comes back from bsstep as `numerics_derivatives_failed`; the kernel prints `bsstep: derivatives failed`, drops the code (the EOS's message is already out through `eos_report`) and returns `envelope_termination` (−2), which every level passes up unchanged and `main` exits 0 on, the "solution diverged" stop; the C API's caller is told the run ended in that mode with valid outputs. The same failure at the accepted point, the kernel's own call after the step, returns its positive code and exits 1. Which of the two a failure meets depends only on where in the step it falls.
  - The comments call every failure but bad input divergence: "any other bsstep failure (the solution diverged) returns envelope_termination" ([:547-549](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L547-L549)), "(bsstep: the solution diverged ...)" ([:75-78](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L75-L78)); only `numerics_step_underflow` is the vanishing step they mean.
  - Related, in atm: `interpolate_allard_surface`'s header says `ierr` is "1 when TeffL is below the table minimum or a polint call fails" ([allard_atmosphere.f90:57-58](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/atm/tables/allard_atmosphere.f90#L57-L58)); a polint failure returns polint's code, `numerics_coincident_points` = 2 ([:254-289](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/atm/tables/allard_atmosphere.f90#L254-L289); polint's code was 1 until [ecce23f0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ecce23f0), 2026-10-29, round 1). Its comment at [:120-122](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/atm/tables/allard_atmosphere.f90#L120-L122) sends the reader to polint's `xa(20)/ya(20)` in `numerics/polint.f90` and to `rotation/shape/rotation_shape_factors.f90`: neither file exists, and polint's arrays are `xa(n)`, `ya(n)`.
  - Correction to the review: the kernel's own call at the step's end is [:879-888](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L879-L888) (:881-884 in the review), and the atmosphere's [:562-571](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L562-L571).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one failure ends one way, as in the F77; a failure of the physics is an error (positive, exit 1, `docs/GUIDELINES.md` "Code style" rule 7), and the clean "solution diverged" stop is kept for the step that vanished, the stop it stands for.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: both calls pass `derivatives_ierr` and, when `jerr == numerics_derivatives_failed`, return it (the EOS's or opacity's own code, whose message is out); `envelope_termination` stays for `numerics_step_underflow`; the comments at :75-78 and :547-549 say which is which; allard's header says "polint's code", and its stale reference goes. Byte-identical on the shipped decks (a converging run does not reach it); a run that fails this way exits 1 instead of 0.

### M133. bsstep accepts a step whose y holds a NaN and returns ierr 0

- **Status:** open. The numerics review's item, confirmed on a scratch copy and corrected (below). Latent: `test_numerics` pins it; whether a deck has accepted such a step is not known.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, as gfortran compiles it: BSSTEP folded the scaled errors with `DMAX1` (Fortran leaves max with a NaN to the processor), which passed over a NaN when another component was finite, and accepted the step; it had no status to report ([bsstep.f:30-36](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/bsstep.f#L30-L36)):
  ```fortran
           ERRMAX = 0.0D0
           DO 30 J = 1,NV
              ERRMAX = DMAX1(ERRMAX,DABS(YERR(J)/YSCAL(J)))
           ERRMAX = ERRMAX/EPS
           IF(ERRMAX.LT.ONE) THEN
  ```
  [278fa171](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/278fa171) (2026-10-11) wrote that behaviour out with `ieee_is_nan` and pinned it, because the 0.03 Msun Debye-Hückel deck's atmosphere, all NaN, must end on step underflow; the `ierr` that now reports the step as a success came with [d874cfcb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d874cfcb) (2026-08-21).
- **Now:** `bsstep`'s error maximum, [bulirsch_stoer.f90:144-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/bulirsch_stoer.f90#L144-L155), and the acceptance, [:156-167](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/bulirsch_stoer.f90#L156-L167); the header's "on success ... y holds the new values", [:62-66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/bulirsch_stoer.f90#L62-L66); the test, [test_numerics.f90:500-515](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/test/test_numerics.f90#L500-L515), and its pin, [expected_test_numerics.out:250](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/test/expected_test_numerics.out#L250) ("NaN in component 3 of 3: ierr 0 ... y(3) is NaN T"); `numerics/README.md` §4, [:72](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/README.md#L72).
- **What is wrong:** when the other components meet the tolerance, a NaN component is passed over, the step is accepted and bsstep returns `ierr` 0 with the NaN in `y` (a scratch build: dy3/dx NaN from x = 0, h = 0.5, gives ierr 0, x = 0.5, y = (0.479, 0.878, NaN)). That is a success it did not have (`docs/GUIDELINES.md` "Code style" rule 7, "never reports a success it did not have"). Correction to the review, which says the envelope catches it because its next derivative call fails: nothing in the envelope tests for a NaN (`envelope_integrands.f90` has no NaN test); the kernel next evaluates its derivatives at the new y ([envelope_integration_kernel.f90:879-888](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L879-L888)), and whether that fails depends on which component is NaN and on the EOS, opacity and gradient routines (a NaN log r does not reach the EOS or the opacity at all).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a step whose result holds a NaN is a failure, reported as one with y as it came in, as bsstep does for its other failures (M57); the caller then decides.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: keep the NaN-skipping maximum (the 0.03 Msun deck's clean stop depends on it, and with every component NaN no step is accepted), but after acceptance return a failure, y and x restored, when any y is NaN (`numerics_bad_input` or a code of its own, which the envelope reports as an error once M132's fix is in); the pin, the header and README §4 change with it. Byte-identical on the shipped decks unless an accepted envelope step there carries a NaN (not measured); `expected_test_numerics.out` changes.

### M134. splint on a decreasing table, which cspline accepts, extrapolates an end interval's cubic with ierr 0

- **Status:** open. The numerics review's item; recomputed (below) on a scratch copy. Latent: every caller's table increases on the shipped decks (rezoning's and the turnover time's depend on the model, M99).
- **In the original F77?** Partly. SPLINT's bisection assumes increasing abscissae, as Numerical Recipes' does, and CSPLINE's header required them ([splint.f:8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/splint.f#L8), [:17-27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/splint.f#L17-L27), [cspline.f:8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/cspline.f#L8)):
  ```fortran
  C (WITH THE XA[I]'S IN ORDER), AND GIVEN THE ARRAY Y2A, WHICH IS THE    ! splint.f
           IF (XA(K) .GT. X) THEN
              KHI = K
  C I.E. Y[I] = F(X[I]) WITH X[1] < X[2] < ... X[N], AND GIVEN VALUES   ! cspline.f
  ```
  [75a98edc](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/75a98edc) (2026-10-29, round 2) made cspline accept a decreasing table as a success ("A decreasing table is allowed"), with the check that pins it, without a matching change to splint.
- **Now:** `cspline`'s header, "strictly monotone (increasing, as splint needs, or decreasing)", [cubic_spline.f90:32-40](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L32-L40), and its order test, which takes either direction, [:56-65](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L56-L65); `splint`, [:110-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L110-L155), whose header ([:113-119](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L113-L119)) states no order and whose bisection ([:134-141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L134-L141)) assumes an increasing one; the check "natural_spline: a decreasing table, the increasing one's y2", [test_numerics.f90:643-647](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/test/test_numerics.f90#L643-L647); `numerics/README.md` §2 and §3 ([:28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/README.md#L28), [:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/README.md#L43): "`cspline`: strictly monotone").
- **What is wrong:** on a decreasing table every step of splint's bisection moves the wrong way, so it always ends on the first or the last interval (klo, khi = 1, 2 or n−1, n) and returns that interval's cubic, extrapolated, with `ierr` 0. With x = (4, 3, 2, 1, 0), y = x² and natural_spline's second derivatives (cspline: ierr 0, the increasing table's y2 reversed), recomputed on a scratch copy: 8.375 at 0.5 (bracket 1, 2; the same spline on the increasing table gives 0.339286, x² 0.25), 4.125 at 1.5 (2.232143), 8.125 at 2.5 (bracket 4, 5; 6.232143) and 20.375 at 3.5 (12.339286, x² 12.25). By hand at 0.5: h = −1, a = −2.5, b = 3.5, y = −40 + 31.5 + (39.375 × 18/7)/6 = 8.375. The README, cspline's header and the pinned check present the decreasing table as supported; only cspline's header says, in passing, that splint needs an increasing one, and splint checks nothing (a decreasing table is not its `numerics_coincident_points`).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a table the spline routines accept as a success is one splint evaluates correctly, or splint says it cannot; a wrong value with ierr 0 is the worst outcome (M99's reasoning).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: splint returns `numerics_bad_input` when xa(n) < xa(1) (one comparison; it has an `ierr`), or bisects in either direction as `locate` does; or cspline refuses a decreasing table again, as the F77 CSPLINE's header required, and the check moves (that reaches the callers only with M99's fix, since none passes cspline's `ierr`). A check and a mutation either way. Byte-identical.

### M135. numerics/README.md's "the cheap preconditions are checked" fails for five routines

- **Status:** open. The numerics review's item, confirmed on a scratch copy; recomputed (below). Latent: the callers pass consistent sizes and increasing tables (simeqc's one caller n + 1 columns, polint's 4 and 2 points, lir's MHD tables).
- **In the original F77?** Yes for each precondition: the F77 routines checked none of them, MEVAL only stated the table's order, POLINT set DY only inside the loop over the N − 1 columns, and LUDCMP indexed A(NP,NP) to N ([meval.f:30](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/meval.f#L30), [polint.f:26](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/polint.f#L26), [:38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/polint.f#L38), [ludcmp.f:16](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/ludcmp.f#L16)):
  ```fortran
  C   XTAB MUST BE INCREASING.                                  ! meval.f
        DO 30 J = 1,N-1                                         ! polint.f
              DY = C(NS+1)
        DIMENSION A(NP,NP)                                      ! ludcmp.f
  ```
  The README's sentence came with [90619ab5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90619ab5), and lir's `y_stride` test with [90475cd2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90475cd2) (both 2026-10-29, round 1).
- **Now:** the sentence, [numerics/README.md:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/README.md#L43) ("The cheap preconditions are checked: sizes, bsstep's limits, the first pivot, the order of a spline's abscissae (`cspline`: strictly monotone; `osplin`: sorted points)"); `osplin`, [quadratic_spline.f90:53-62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L53-L62) (the header) and [:73-88](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L73-L88) (its checks); `simeqc`, [linear_solvers.f90:177-264](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L177-L264); `ludcmp`, [:47-131](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L47-L131); `polint`, [table_interpolation.f90:137-190](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L137-L190); `lir`, [:203-231](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L203-L231).
- **What is wrong:** the sentence holds for cspline, osplin's evaluation points, lir's point count and bsstep's limits, not for these, which return ierr 0 or index past their arrays:
  - `osplin`'s table order: the header requires xtab nondecreasing ([:53-54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L53-L54)) and nothing checks it. With x = (4, 3, 2, 1, 0), y = x², recomputed on a scratch copy: 2.875 at 1.5 and 6.375 at 2.5 (x²: 2.25 and 6.25; the increasing table gives 2.265625 and 6.256944), and it does not even return the nodes: 10 at x = 4 (y = 16), 2 at x = 0 (y = 0). M100 is the repeated-node case.
  - `simeqc`'s num_cols > num_unknowns: the header says the columns past A hold the right-hand sides ([:179-181](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L179-L181)). With num_cols = num_unknowns the back substitution ([:254-263](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L254-L263)) treats A's last column as one: A = [[2, 1], [1, 3]] returns ierr 0 with its second column overwritten by (0, 1) (scratch copy). Below it the loops index columns past `a(num_unknowns, num_cols)`.
  - `ludcmp`'s 1 ≤ n ≤ np: `a(np,np)` is indexed to n ([:51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L51), [:63-67](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L63-L67)), and n = 0 reaches `a(0,0)` at [:130](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/linear_solvers.f90#L130).
  - `polint`'s n ≥ 1, and its dy at n = 1: dy (`intent(out)`) is set only inside the loop over n − 1 columns ([:168-189](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L168-L189)), so at n = 1 it is undefined with ierr 0 (scratch copy: at -O0 the caller's value stays; at -O3 gfortran 15 treats the argument as clobbered and the caller read 0); n = 0 reads xa(1) and ya(1) of empty arrays ([:153-164](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L153-L164)).
  - `lir`'s sizes: it compares `y_stride`, which it uses nowhere else, with size(table_y, 1) ([:228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L228)), and not `num_y`, which indexes table_y and result_y, nor `num_points` with table_z and table_y. M101 is its repeated-abscissa case.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the README is the contract a caller reads; a precondition it calls checked is checked, and one that is not is named in the routine's header.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: one comparison each (osplin's xtab order, simeqc's num_cols > num_unknowns, ludcmp's 1 ≤ n ≤ np, polint's n ≥ 1 with dy = 0 at n = 1, lir's num_y and num_points against the arrays, and drop `y_stride`), each with a check and a mutation; or narrow the sentence to the checks that exist. Byte-identical.

### M136. The SCV reader never compares the He and Z tables' grid with the H table's, and the OPAL 1995 reader accepts a zero T6

- **Status:** fixed in [53563ab8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/53563ab8) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos), byte-identical. The eos review's item, with an addition (the He and Z tables' pressures, below). Latent: the shipped SCV tables share one grid (checked), and no deck uses OPAL 1995. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. SETUPS read the He and Z tables' row headers into dummies, on the comment that the grids are the same, and READCO left its T6 loop at a zero, where READCOEOS06 stopped with an error ([setups.f:311-322](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setups.f#L311-L322), [readco.f:90-97](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readco.f#L90-L97), [readcoeos06.f:98-105](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readcoeos06.f#L98-L105)):
  ```fortran
              READ(ISCVHE,1) DUM1,DUM2                                ! setups.f
              READ(ISCVZ,1) DUM3,DUM4
  C TABLE GRID POINTS IN T, P(T) ARE THE SAME - NPTSY AND TLOGX
          IF(T6LIST(1,I) .EQ. 0.0D0) THEN                             ! readco.f
            NTUSE=I
            GO TO 14
  ```
  (`NTUSE` was set and read nowhere.)
- **Now:** `read_scv_rows`, [scv_eos.f90:898-936](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L898-L936): the He and Z tables' log T and point count into `copy_log10_t` and `copy_npts` ([:909-911](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L909-L911)), their rows at [:917](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L917) and [:923](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L923), the message at [:929-935](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L929-L935); `read_scv_tables`' header, [:865-866](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L865-L866). `readco`, [opal95_eos.f90:947-1106](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L947-L1106), its T6 grid at [:1007-1014](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L1007-L1014); `readcoeos`' check for 2001 and 2006, [opal_eos.f90:881-888](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L881-L888); README §3, [README.md:68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L68).
- **What is wrong:**
  - The He and Z tables' log T and point count for each T row are read and dropped, and their points' log P (column 1) is read into `tabley` and `tablez` and never used: the H table's grid (`tlogx`, `nptsx`, `tablex(:,:,1)`) serves all three. A He or Z table on another grid is read misaligned without a word; when a read does fail, the message names the H table whichever failed.
  - In `readco` a zero T6 in density column 1 ends the loop: `t6_grid` keeps zeros from that row on (zero-filled static storage), and the spacings become 1/(0 − T6) < 0 at that row and 1/(0 − 0) beyond, which `-ffpe-trap=zero` stops on and a release build carries as infinities into the interpolation. The 2001/2006 reader rejects the same table with `ierr = 1` and a message.
  - README §3 says every reader checks its reads.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a reader rejects a table it cannot use, with its message (M69's and M75's rule).
- **What we did:** `read_scv_rows` compares the He and Z tables' log T, point counts and log P_gas with the H table's and names the table off grid; `readco`'s zero T6 is an error, as the 2001/2006 reader's is (since [dc8755e1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dc8755e1) OPAL 1995 is read by `readcoeos` too). Byte-identical. The read-failure message that names the H table whichever failed is reworded with eos's messages (B list: eos item 7).

### M137. saha_log10t_cutoff is never range-checked, and below 5.7 the fully ionized gas extrapolates the Fermi-Dirac table

- **Status:** fixed in [589b71ea](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/589b71ea) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos), byte-identical. The eos review's item, corrected (every deck sets the control, below). Latent: all 1,159 inlists set it to 6.0, the default. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQRELV finds the table's T row the same way, and PARMIN reads `TSCUT` from the deck unchecked ([eqrelv.f:56-62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqrelv.f#L56-L62), [parmin.f:325](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L325), [:397-398](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L397-L398)):
  ```fortran
        JT1 = INT(5.0D0*(TL - 5.0D0))
        JT1 = MAX0(1,MIN0(JT1,18))  ! Force jt1 to be in the table
        TTUD = 5.0D0*(TL8 - (5.0D0 + 0.20D0*DFLOAT(JT1)))
  ```
- **Now:** `start_fully_ionized_solution`, [yale_eos.f90:733-737](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L733-L737); `gas_eos`, which evaluates the fully ionized gas at and above the cutoff and across the 0.5 dex below it ([blended_eos.f90:241-259](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L241-L259)); the control, [eos_configuration.f90:36-39](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_configuration.f90#L36-L39); `eos_init`'s checks, [eos_lib.f90:101-118](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_lib.f90#L101-L118); README §4, [README.md:73](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L73).
- **What is wrong:** the Fermi-Dirac table's 20 T rows are at log T = 5 + 0.2j, j = 1 to 20 (the file holds no T; the row formula defines it), so its first row is log T 5.2. Below that `jt1` is clamped to 1 and the offset `ttud` goes negative, and the table is extrapolated quadratically in log T. The fully ionized gas is evaluated wherever log T > cutoff − 0.5, so a cutoff below 5.7 extrapolates silently: `eos_init` checks the OPAL vintage and the Debye-Hückel range but not the cutoff, and README §4 gives no range. The extrapolation is probably mild: the table's entries are close to linear in log T over its first rows (third differences of at most 0.002, at its most degenerate abscissa), and the review's scratch run with cutoff 5.0 (log T 5.0 to 5.3, log P 9) gives a density within 2.5e-5 of the ideal gas's; degenerate points were not measured. The review's "no shipped deck sets the control" does not hold: all 1,159 inlists set `saha_log10t_cutoff = 6.0`, the default; none sets another value.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a control whose range a table limits says so, and is refused outside it.
