- **What we did:** `eos_init` refuses a cutoff below 5.7 (the table's first row, log T 5.2, plus the ramp), `ierr = 1` with a message; README §3 states the Fermi-Dirac table's range ([72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0)). Byte-identical.

### M138. The history, profile, pulsation and isochrone writes and the copy of the deck have no error path, and write_gsm_pulse ignores HDF5's status after the create

- **Status:** fixed in [ffd5ce50](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ffd5ce50) (2026-10-31, round 3), with M110. Byte-identical. Corrected (below): under gfortran a full disk is not a runtime error but a silent cut. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. The F77's writers had no `IOSTAT` either, the isochrone record and the pulsation model among them ([wrtout.f:610-612](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtout.f#L610-L612), [wrtmod.f:192-193](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmod.f#L192-L193)), and no F77 reader had an error path:
  ```fortran
            WRITE(IISO,1005)MODEL,YRAGE,ERGPSL,CMR,XKTEFF,CMPSQS,YCENTER,   ! wrtout.f
       *      GMHECORE
           WRITE (IOPMOD, 5001) MODEL,IDM,IPVER,QSMASS,                     ! wrtmod.f
       1         TEFFL,BL,TEMPR, DAGE, CMIXL, XENV0, ZENV0
  ```
  The other writers are 2026's: the interior GYRE file [9df62b7e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9df62b7e) (2026-08-20), the history, the profiles and FGONG [eb624a69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/eb624a69) (2026-08-22), GSM [ec77ad33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ec77ad33) (2026-08-23), the copy of the deck [b38ec9c3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b38ec9c3) (2026-08-28). [a9de5f99](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a9de5f99) (2026-10-11) gave their opens `check_io` and left the writes.
- **Now:** each writer opens through `check_io` and then writes without `iostat`:
  - `write_history_row`: the open at [history_output.f90:321-324](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/history_output.f90#L321-L324); the header and the row at [:331-356](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/history_output.f90#L331-L356); the flush at [:359](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/history_output.f90#L359);
  - `write_profile`: [profile_output.f90:68-104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/profile_output.f90#L68-L104);
  - `write_fgong_pulse`: [pulsation_output.f90:76-136](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L76-L136); `write_gyre_pulse`: [:248-253](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L248-L253);
  - `write_gsm_pulse`: `h5fcreate_f`'s status is checked ([:174-176](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L174-L176)); `h5open_f`'s ([:173](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L173)) and every later call's, the five attributes, the datasets and the closes, are overwritten unread ([:178-196](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L178-L196));
  - the isochrone record and card header: [yrec_output.f90:163-165](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L163-L165), [:313-315](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L313-L315);
  - `copy_inlists_used`: [run_files.f90:270-279](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/run_files.f90#L270-L279).

  `io/README.md` says io reports through "`check_io` after an open, read or write" ([README.md:85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L85), §3; and [:31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L31)).
- **What is wrong:** none of these 31 write statements and the flush has an `iostat` (nor has any of io's 45 data-file writes, the `.mod`'s 14 of M110 included; counted over the joined statements). A failed write or flush ends the run in a Fortran runtime error (exit 2, no `ERROR:` line in the run log), where a failed open or read is reported through `check_io` and exits 1. For GSM it is silent: a failed attribute or dataset call leaves a damaged file, HDF5 prints its error stack to stderr, and `write_gsm_pulse` returns `ierr` 0, so the run goes on; a failed create returns without `h5close_f`. The README's "or write" holds for no write: every `check_io(..., 'write', ...)` in io follows an open.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a failed write is reported like a failed open ("ERROR: cannot write <path>: <reason>"), exit 1 (L5's and M23's rule, and M110's fix for the `.mod`).
- **What we did:** `io/output_files.f90`: `open_output_file`, and `close_output_file`, which reports the first failed write, closes the unit and compares the file's size on disk with what the unit wrote; every write of the history, profile, FGONG, GYRE, isochrone and deck-copy writers takes `iostat`/`iomsg` and skips the writes after the first failure; `write_gsm_pulse` checks each HDF5 call and closes the file and the library on a failure; `output_run_header`, `output_close` and the Monte Carlo writers return `ierr`. Measured on a 2 MB disk image: gfortran 15.2 reports nothing when a formatted write fills the disk (every write, the flush and the close return `iostat` 0, the file is cut short and the run ends with exit 0; libgfortran's buffered write ignores its flush's result), the same under `RLIMIT_FSIZE`. So the size check is the full-disk detector: "ERROR: cannot write <path>: the file on disk is shorter than what was written to it (is the disk full?)", exit 1. It covers the files io closes (the profiles, the pulsation files, the copy of the deck, the history at the run's end); the `.mod` and the isochrone file, open for the run, check each write but not their size (M173). Nine `test_io` checks (a unit open for reading, a directory that cannot be made, a full disk through `RLIMIT_FSIZE`) and two `test_error_exit` cases; 15 mutations caught.

### M139. compute_neutrino_fluxes without calc_neutrinos writes a neutrino-flux table of zeros, without a warning

- **Status:** open. The net review's item. Latent: no shipped deck sets `compute_neutrino_fluxes` (no file under testsuite/, examples/, sample_cases/, grid/ or startmodels/ names it).
- **In the original F77?** Partly. ENGEB computed the fluxes only with LSNU, and MAIN's per-shell table (MHP 2/04) read them after each ENGEB call, but the table was switched off in the source, so no deck could ask for it ([main.f:324-325](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L324-L325), [:365-376](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L365-L376), [engeb.f:1052](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L1052)):
  ```fortran
        LNUTAB = .FALSE.                                          ! main.f
        IF(LNUTAB)THEN
              FLUXI0(J,I) = FLUX(J)*HS2(I)
        IF(LSNU)THEN                                              ! engeb.f
  ```
  The control came with [955a50c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/955a50c7) (2026-08-23), which made the table "a real opt-in diagnostic" without tying it to `calc_neutrinos` (it is the table M82's fix touched).
- **Now:** `write_neutrino_flux_table`, [neutrino_flux_output.f90:39-140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L39-L140): its header names only `compute_neutrino_fluxes` ([:20-38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L20-L38)); the per-shell loop takes `burn%neutrino_flux` and `burn%be7_mass_fraction` from `compute_zone_energy` ([:79-99](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L79-L99)), then the totals ([:101-103](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L101-L103)) and the profile ([:105-138](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L105-L138)); its call, for each kind card's starting model, under `physics%compute_neutrino_fluxes` alone ([run_driver.f90:388-393](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L388-L393)); `compute_nuclear_energy`, which fills the fluxes and X(⁷Be) only with `calc_neutrinos` ([nuclear_energy.f90:137-138](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L137-L138), the record's zeros at [:56-59](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L56-L59)); the registry rows ([controls_registry.tsv:388](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L388), [:190](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L190)); `check_controls` ([controls_check.f90:62-112](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_check.f90#L62-L112)) and `warn_inconsistent_controls`, for "combinations that are silently inert" ([:136-184](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_check.f90#L136-L184)), neither with a rule for it.
- **What is wrong:** with `compute_neutrino_fluxes = .true.` and `calc_neutrinos = .false.` (its default), the table is written, but every flux column, the ten totals and the X(⁷Be) column are zero: the per-shell lines carry only the index and the shell mass, the profile lines only r, T₆, log n_e and the mass. Nothing says why. The registry row (repeated by `physics.defaults` and `controls_registry.md`) describes the control as writing "the per-zone solar neutrino production table" with no word of `calc_neutrinos`, and its name says it computes the fluxes; only net/README §3 ([:142](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/README.md#L142)) says that the fluxes depend on `calc_neutrinos`. The row also says "at the start of each run", where the table is written for each kind card's starting model.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a combination that silently produces nothing is what `warn_inconsistent_controls` is for, and a control's name and description say what it does (M52's rule).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `warn_inconsistent_controls` warns when `compute_neutrino_fluxes` is on and `calc_neutrinos` off (requiring `calc_neutrinos` instead would change such a deck's history columns); the registry row and the routine's header name the dependence and say "each kind card". No output changes but the warning, on a deck that sets the combination (none shipped).

### M140. The deck's atmosphere choice has three star homes, the atm builder copies the run copy, and the copy check misses the read's copy

- **Status:** fixed in [3a44ae33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3a44ae33), [74beeaba](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/74beeaba) and [f8746f4a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f8746f4a) (2026-10-31, round 3). Byte-identical; the controls test's pins changed a label only. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. The F77 had two homes: PARMIN copies the deck's `KTTAU` into `KTTAU0` and clears `LTTAU`, SURFBC switches `KTTAU` to the gray atmosphere and back to `KTTAU0`, and SETUPS, called once after PARMIN, loads the tables of `KTTAU` before any switch ([parmin.f:750-753](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L750-L753), [surfbc.f:68-77](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/surfbc.f#L68-L77), [setups.f:196](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setups.f#L196), [main.f:206-208](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L206-L208)):
  ```fortran
        KTTAU0 = KTTAU                                         ! parmin.f
        LTTAU = .FALSE.
           IF(KTTAU0.EQ.3.AND.TEFFL.LT.3.95D0)THEN             ! surfbc.f
              KTTAU = KTTAU0
        IF ((KTTAU .EQ. 3) .OR. (KTTAU .EQ. 4)) THEN           ! setups.f
  ```
  The third home came with [d86d5dce](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d86d5dce) (2026-10-30, the controls split): `physics%atm_choice` became a control the run never changes, the working value moved to the run copy `atm_choice_in_use`, the builder (which had copied `s%job%atm_choice`) was pointed at the run copy, and `atm_choice_initial` (`KTTAU0`) stayed.
- **Now:** `atm_choice_initial`, [star_info_lib.f90:217-219](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L217-L219), set from the legacy `kttau` by `adopt_canonical_names` ([controls_reader.f90:190-192](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_reader.f90#L190-L192)), before `derive_controls`; the control, stored after it ([controls_sync.f90:655](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_sync.f90#L655)), and the run copy armed from it ([:836](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_sync.f90#L836); the member, [star_info_lib.f90:357-364](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L357-L364)); the buffer's comment, [controls_buffer.f90:249-252](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L249-L252); the switch back to `atm_choice_initial`, [surface_boundary.f90:150-166](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/structure/surface_boundary.f90#L150-L166); `atm_settings_from_star` ("atm's settings from the controls"), which copies the run copy into the field that selects `atm_init`'s tables, [microphysics_settings.f90:156-170](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/setup/microphysics_settings.f90#L156-L170), [atm_lib.f90:51-66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L51-L66); the copy check `check_control_copies`, [check_boundaries.py:608-616](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L608-L616), which skips the read's files ([:452-456](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L452-L456), [:651-656](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L651-L656)); what the docs say it checks, [state/README.md:454](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/README.md#L454) and [GUIDELINES.md:293-298](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/docs/GUIDELINES.md#L293-L298).
- **What is wrong:**
  - Since the split the control `physics%atm_choice` keeps the deck's value for the whole run, so `atm_choice_initial` is a second copy of it, read only by the switch back. The two are set at different points of the read (the copy from `kttau` before `derive_controls`, the control from the buffer after it), so a derivation of the choice added there would leave them apart.
  - `atm_settings_from_star` wants the deck's choice ("which tables atm_init loads", [atm_tables.f90:15-18](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/atm/atm_tables.f90#L15-L18)) and copies the run copy, which the surface boundary and the envelope integration switch ([envelope_integration.f90:191-192](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L191-L192)). The two agree because `install_run_settings` runs once, from `prepare_run` right after `read_controls` ([run_driver.f90:138](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L138), [:151](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L151); [run_setup.f90:114](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/run_setup.f90#L114)), as SETUPS did. The review's concern holds in form only: a re-install after a switch would read no table, but `atm_init` clears none, so the tables already read would still serve the switch back.
  - state/README §6 lists among what `check_boundaries.py` checks that "any other copy of a control into a star member is in a module its comment names, with the control named", and GUIDELINES says it "enforces all of it". The check looks only at `s%m = s%control%x` and `s%m = s%physics%x` outside the read's eight files, so the read's one such copy, `s%atm_choice_initial = kttau` (from the legacy name, `legacy_controls.f90`, not a buffer name as the review says), is never checked, and its comment would fail the check: on a scratch copy, the same copy made in `run_setup` (`s%atm_choice_initial = s%physics%atm_choice`) is reported twice, for a comment that names neither `physics%atm_choice` nor `run_setup`. Made inside the read, even from `s%physics%atm_choice`, it passes. The check's docstring states the exemption ("outside the read and the tests"); the README and GUIDELINES do not.
  - The read's reset of the latch `use_ttau_relation` repeats what the template star gives every run; it is PARMIN's `LTTAU = .FALSE.` and harmless.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the deck's choice has one home, the control ("the control keeps the deck's value", GUIDELINES, "The controls"), and whatever means the deck's choice reads it; a check's documented reach is its reach.
- **What we did:** `atm_choice` has one home, the control: `atm_choice_initial`, the read's copy into it and the read's reset of `use_ttau_relation` are gone, and the surface boundary's switch back reads `s%physics%atm_choice` (3a44ae33); `atm_settings_from_star` copies the deck's choice, which selects `atm_init`'s tables (74beeaba); `check_control_copies` also checks the controls read's own copies of a control into a star member, which must name the module and the control, and no run copy may be set there (f8746f4a); a writer that a run copy's comment names may restore it from its own control, as the switch back does (3a44ae33). The dump's `star%atm_choice_initial` is `physics%atm_choice` now, with the same value in every deck.

### M141. check_boundaries cannot see pure procedures, so PUBLIC["net"] checks 2 of its 9 entries

- **Status:** open (tool). The net review's item, recounted with a copy of the regex (below). The boundary checker; no output.
- **In the original F77?** No. `DEF_RE` came in its present form with [500b5a9f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/500b5a9f) (2026-08-21) and the `net` key of `PUBLIC` with [7adda701](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7adda701) (2026-08-22), today's names with [cfd4b460](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/cfd4b460) (2026-10-10). net's entries became `pure` with [31fe9ba4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/31fe9ba4) and [ef4c50f1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ef4c50f1) (2026-10-11) and `compute_nuclear_energy` with [78f58053](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/78f58053) (2026-10-29, round 1), after which the pattern no longer saw them; README:11's sentence came with [90d041e0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90d041e0) (2026-10-29, round 1).
- **Now:** `DEF_RE`, [check_boundaries.py:116-121](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L116-L121); the call check in `main`, [:917-938](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L917-L938), which skips a `call` of any name `DEF_RE` did not record ([:933-935](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L933-L935)); `PUBLIC["net"]`, [:82-90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L82-L90); the docstring, [:4-5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L4-L5); [net/README.md:11](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/README.md#L11).
- **What is wrong:** `DEF_RE` matches `[recursive] subroutine`, `function` and `double precision|integer|logical function`, no `pure` or `elemental` prefix and no other type-spec. A copy of the pattern run over src/ at d6a66ffe (`python3 -B`, beside a count of every procedure whatever its prefix) records 5 of net's 63 procedures (58 are `pure` or `elemental`), and of `PUBLIC["net"]`'s 9 entries only `set_net_settings` and `cross_section_scales_from_sstandard`; `compute_network_rates`, `burn_implicitly`, `compute_abundance_rates`, `compute_nuclear_energy`, `deuterium_rate`, `burn_deuterium_region` and `compute_li_be_rates` are invisible. So a cross-domain `call` of any pure net procedure passes, listed or not: only the facade check (`FACADE_ONLY_DOMAINS`) protects net, and it bounds outside callers to what `net_lib` re-exports, so a procedure newly re-exported and called from outside passes the `PUBLIC` check unseen. atm has 3 of its 8 entries visible; every other listed domain's entries are visible. With the prefixes accepted, the call check reports no violation today (same copy). Even then `deuterium_rate`, a function, stays unchecked: `CALL_RE` sees `call` statements only, so no function reference is checked in any domain (atm's five invisible entries are functions too, so for atm the pattern's fix changes nothing). The docstring says the tool enforces that "a file outside a physics domain may only call that domain's *public* entry points"; README:11 says it "lists the procedures others may call (`PUBLIC["net"]`)" beside the facade rule it does enforce. The same kind as M116, the star tools' header pattern.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a checker checks the list it holds; one that passes what it claims to reject is worse than none (M116).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `DEF_RE` accepts any sequence of the prefixes `pure`, `elemental`, `impure`, `recursive`, `module` and a type-spec before `function`, as M116 proposes for `PROC_RE`; the docstring and README:11 say that function references are not checked (or `CALL_RE` gains them). No output changes; the check passes as it is.

### M142. math/README.md's usage rule is not the checker's: `x**n` refused, parameters not exempt, `x**(2-a)` and `x**((a))` let through

- **Status:** open (tool). The math review's item, confirmed on a scratch copy of the checker. The checker and the README; no output. M124 holds three other math statements.
- **In the original F77?** No. The `**` test came with [79631678](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/79631678) (2026-08-30), the parameter exemption, for the elementary functions only, with [529d3fb3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/529d3fb3) (2026-10-11), and README §3 with [023d5080](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/023d5080) (2026-10-29, round 1).
- **Now:** `check_math_lib`, [check_boundaries.py:840-914](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L840-L914): its docstring ([:841-847](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L841-L847)), the parameter filter ([:850-861](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L850-L861)) applied to `code_kept` only ([:869-870](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L869-L870)), and the `**` test over `code_lines` ([:903-913](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L903-L913)); the rule, [math/README.md:37](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/README.md#L37), against §2's table, [:25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/README.md#L25).
- **What is wrong:** run on synthetic files (a copy of the checker and of math_lib in a scratch tree):
  - "Integer exponents (`x**2`, `x**n`) ... stay as `**`": `y = x**n` with `integer :: n` is refused (`real-exponent **`), since every token after `**` that is not all digits counts as real. math_lib's own comment says `pow(x, iy)` exists for integer-typed sites ([math_lib.f90:24-27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/math_lib.f90#L24-L27)).
  - "Parameter initializers are exempt": the exemption covers the elementary-function test, not the `**` test, so `real(dp), parameter :: c_param = 2.0d0**0.5d0` is refused.
  - The `**` test reads only the first token after `**` and one optional `(`: `x**(2-a)` passes (the token is 2) and `x**((a))` passes (no token matches), each a real exponent, that is a libm pow that bypasses crmath; `x**(2.5d0*a)` and `x**a` are refused. None is in the code today (`check_math_lib` reports nothing on src/; `**((` occurs only in the integer `2.0d0**((max_stage_index-extrap_order)/2)` at [bulirsch_stoer.f90:170](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/bulirsch_stoer.f90#L170), which passes the same way), and nothing tests the checker on such a case.
  - "Integer exponents ... are exact repeated multiplication": §2's table says the intrinsic backend's integer power is the compiler's power by squaring, and neither is exact beyond n = 2 (each multiplication rounds).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the README states the rule the checker enforces, and the checker refuses every real exponent it is there to refuse; a newcomer who follows either should not be refused for compliant code nor let through with a hidden pow.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: the README says that integer variables go through `pow(x, n)` (or the checker accepts names declared integer), that parameter initializers are not exempt from the `**` rule (or the checker exempts them there too), and "power by squaring" as in §2; the `**` test reads the whole exponent, a parenthesized one to its closing parenthesis, and accepts only integer literals and integer names (`tools/migrate_math_phase1.py`'s `decl_types` already reads the declarations); `test_boundaries.py` gains synthetic cases for `x**(2-a)`, `x**((a))`, `x**n` and a parameter initializer. No output changes.

### M143. state/README lists a contract-coverage check that does not exist, and the checker's docstring still describes a global star

- **Status:** fixed in [2c09e12b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2c09e12b) (2026-10-31, round 3). No output. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The claim came with [737c00a1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/737c00a1) (2026-10-29, round 2), a minute after [10d42185](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/10d42185) put contracts on every core/run and core/step driver; the docstring's "global `star`" with [802b3cdb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/802b3cdb) (2026-10-13), stale since [c35778aa](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c35778aa) (2026-10-28) removed the global star.
- **Now:** [state/README.md:453](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/README.md#L453): `test_boundaries.py` runs `check_star_contracts.py` ("the declared `star reads:` / `star writes:` lists match the code; every procedure of `core/run/` and `core/step/` that takes the star declares them, ..."); the checker's docstring, [check_star_contracts.py:4-7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_star_contracts.py#L4-L7) and [:31-33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_star_contracts.py#L31-L33) ("The check is opt-in: only procedures that carry the two lines are checked"); its `main`, which skips a procedure without them ([:387-396](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/check_star_contracts.py#L387-L396)); `test_star_contracts`, [test_boundaries.py:22-29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/test_boundaries.py#L22-L29).
- **What is wrong:** nothing checks that a star-taking procedure of core/run or core/step declares a contract: one without the lines is skipped. Recounted with a copy of the review's script and with an independent scan of the procedure headers, both against d6a66ffe: core/run 22 of 22 and core/step 25 of 25 (47 of 47), setup/ 14 of 14; 64 contracts in all, as the checker counts, the other three in io/, core/model and core/structure. With `apply_monte_carlo_parameters`' contract deleted on a scratch copy, `check_star_contracts.py` passes ("Star contracts OK (63 declared)"), and so do `check_boundaries.py` and `gen_star_docs.py --check`. The docstring says the contracts cover reads "through the global `star`, or through the argument `s` (type(star_info)) that core's procedures receive it as"; since 2026-10-28 there is no global star (`STAR_ACCESS_BUDGET` keeps it at zero), and io/, rotation/ and setup/ take `s` too.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a README's list of checks is what the tests enforce; a newcomer who adds a core/run driver without a contract is told the tests will catch it.
- **What we did:** `check_star_contracts.py`'s `REQUIRED_DIRS` (core/run, core/step, setup and io; the generated `io/controls_sync.f90` exempt) makes the two lines required there: a star-taking procedure without them fails the check, which says how to add them. io's 31 star-taking procedures without a contract gained theirs (comment lines, filled by `--fix`), and the merge two more (`open_run_files(s, ierr)` and `output_directory(s)`, [b7348468](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b7348468)). The docstring describes the argument-only star and how the two tools differ on an `intent(inout)` argument. Four mutations caught; the self-test covers the rule.

### M144. test_eos's "the record's defaults are the controls'" compares the record with literals

- **Status:** fixed (test) in [330bcf04](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/330bcf04) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos). The eos review's item, with an addition (two switches unchecked). The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The record's defaults and the check came with M72's fix, [65ca207c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/65ca207c) (2026-10-29, round 2).
- **Now:** the check, [test_eos.f90:1028-1033](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L1028-L1033); `eos_settings_t`, [eos_configuration.f90:22-40](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_configuration.f90#L22-L40), whose header says its defaults are the controls' ([:7-10](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_configuration.f90#L7-L10)); the controls' defaults in [physics.defaults](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults) ([:137](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L137), [:141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L141), [:279](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L279), [:291](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L291), [:375](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L375), [:439](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L439), [:516](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L516), [:584](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/physics.defaults#L584)); README §4 ([README.md:73](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L73)) and §6 ([:107](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L107)).
- **What is wrong:** the check compares `eos_settings_t()` with 6, −1, 1, `opal_vintage_none` and false, written in the test, not with the controls' defaults. If a default in `physics.defaults` changes, `eos_settings_t` keeps the old one and the check still passes, so "Its defaults are the controls'" holds only as long as both are edited by hand: M72 was that defect, and its check would not catch it again. It also leaves out two of the record's switches, `use_diffusion_z` and `use_numerical_derivatives`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a check named after a property tests it against its source.
- **What we did:** `test_eos.py`'s `test_eos_settings_defaults_are_the_controls` compares `eos_settings_t`'s declared defaults with `physics.defaults` through the registry's settings column. No output changes.

### M145. No check covers pow_i's zero-base branch under crmath

- **Status:** open (test). The math review's item, confirmed on a scratch crmath build. The test; no output.
- **In the original F77?** No; `math_lib` is 2026. The zero-base check came with [c2638e4b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c2638e4b) (2026-10-29, round 1) and the mutations with [42048e86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/42048e86) (2026-10-29, round 2).
- **Now:** `pow_i`'s branch, [math_lib.f90:95-98](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/math_lib.f90#L95-L98); the zero-base checks, [test_math.f90:114-123](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/test/test_math.f90#L114-L123); the two zero-base mutations, both of `pow_r`'s branch, [mutate_math.py:52-54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/test/mutate_math.py#L52-L54) and [:64-66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/test/mutate_math.py#L64-L66); `math/README.md` §2, "each is checked by `test_math`", [:18-24](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/math/README.md#L18-L24).
- **What is wrong:** the branch is what makes §2's pow(0, 0) = 0 and pow(0, y < 0) = 0 hold for integer exponents under crmath. The checks use real exponents for 0 and −1, and the one integer case, pow(0.0d0, 3), is 0 with or without the branch. On a scratch crmath build (`test_math.f90` and `math_lib.f90` copied, the branch deleted, built as the Makefile's `test_math_crmath`): pow(0.0d0, 0) = 1 and pow(0.0d0, −1) = +Inf, and all ten crmath checks print ok, the output identical to the pinned `expected_test_math_crmath.out`. So §2's "each is checked by `test_math`" does not hold for an integer exponent. The branch's lines run (pow(0.0d0, 3) takes it), so the README's 100% coverage does not show it either.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** every MESA-definition branch §2 lists is checked, under the backend it belongs to, and caught by a mutation (README §5).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: add pow(0.0d0, 0) and pow(0.0d0, −1) to each backend's zero-base check (crmath 0 and 0; intrinsic 1 and +Inf), and a mutation of pow_i's branch to `mutate_math.py` (18 mutations then). No output outside the test.

### M146. The timestep limiter's hydrogen-burning luminosity sums channels 1 to 4 by number, which the "Add a chain" recipe does not mention

- **Status:** open (doc). The net review's item, checked (the dummy's shape and channel 9, below). Latent: today channels 1-4 are the four hydrogen chains; a hydrogen-burning chain added by the recipe is left out of L_H.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, the literal indices. HTIMER summed TLUMX(1) to (4) for the hydrogen limit and gated the helium limit on TLUMX(5), and CRRECT's log line summed TLUMX(1)-(4) and TLUMX(5) + TLUMX(8), on an 8-element TLUMX ([htimer.f:24](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/htimer.f#L24), [:101](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/htimer.f#L101), [:112](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/htimer.f#L112), [crrect.f:204-205](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/crrect.f#L204-L205)):
  ```fortran
       *     HCOMP(15,JSON),EG(6),TLUMX(8),HP(JSON),HR(JSON),OMEGA(JSON) ! htimer.f
        HYDLUM = TLUMX(1) + TLUMX(2) + TLUMX(3) + TLUMX(4)
        IF(TLUMX(5).GT.1.0D-34)THEN
           TLUMH = TLUMX(1) + TLUMX(2) + TLUMX(3) + TLUMX(4)          ! crrect.f
           TLUMHE= TLUMX(5) + TLUMX(8)
  ```
  The ninth channel, `i_lum_extra`, came with [6fc1a3f8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6fc1a3f8) (2026-10-28); the chain recipe with [90d041e0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90d041e0) (round 1) and its step 4 as it reads now with [90d39ba2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90d39ba2) (round 2, both 2026-10-29), after [b2f0ece2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b2f0ece2) had put the two renormalizations on one loop because "the 'add a chain' recipe did not name henyey_iteration".
- **Now:** `compute_timestep`, [timestep_control.f90:48-243](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L48-L243): the dummy `luminosity_components(8)` ([:70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L70)); L_grav as component 7 ([:123](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L123)); `limit_by_hydrogen_burning`, L_H = components 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 ([:169-181](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L169-L181)), which the shell branch of `timestep_limit_hburn` divides by ([:476-477](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L476-L477)); `limit_by_helium_burning`'s gate on component 5 ([:187-195](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L187-L195)); the actual, `s%luminosity_breakdown_lsun`, from both callers ([step_driver.f90:226-228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L226-L228), [run_driver.f90:419-423](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L419-L423)); the channels, `n_lum_channels` = 9 ([star_info_lib.f90:87-94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L87-L94)); the Henyey log line's hand sums ([henyey_iteration.f90:363-366](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/structure/henyey_iteration.f90#L363-L366)) and its channels 6-7 by number ([:379-381](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/structure/henyey_iteration.f90#L379-L381)); the recipe, [net/README.md:182-187](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/README.md#L182-L187).
- **What is wrong:**
  - The recipe gives a new chain the channel `n_lum_channels` + 1 and says that `eps_total` sums every chain and that the two renormalizations sum every channel through `luminosity_channel_sum`. Neither the timestep limiter nor the log line follows: L_H is channels 1-4 by number, and the log line's hydrogen and helium sums name four and two channels. A hydrogen-burning chain added by the recipe (the recipe's own trace made a chain for hep, [README:167](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/README.md#L167); or the CNO cycle split into CN and NO) is left out of L_H, so the shell-burning limit E_H atime(itime_dx_total) X_surf M☉/(L_H L☉) allows a longer step, and with L_H below 1e-34 L☉ the hydrogen limit is off; the log line under-reports. The core branch uses the luminosity at the core edge, not L_H.
  - The dummy is explicit-shape, 8 elements, while the actual has `n_lum_channels` = 9: legal by sequence association (the dummy is not longer than the actual), and it hides channel 9, `i_lum_extra`, the extra energy sources' channel. That one does not burn, so nothing changes today; a new chain's channel 10 would be outside the dummy too.
  - The helium gate keys on component 5, triple α alone, as YTIME's did, while the log line counts triple α and the α captures (`i_lum_he_c`): the F77's choice, kept, but by number.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a chain's burning group (hydrogen or helium) is data the chain carries, and a group's luminosity is one sum over its channels that the limiter and the log line share, as `luminosity_channel_sum` serves the two renormalizations (b2f0ece2's reason).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: a burning group per chain in network's chain data, exported by `net_lib`; one star-layer sum over the channels of a group, used by `limit_by_hydrogen_burning` and the log line (and by the helium gate, if the α captures should open it: a results decision); `i_lum_*` names for components 5 and 7, the dummy sized `n_lum_channels`; the recipe names `timestep_control` and the log line. Byte-identical with the helium gate kept on triple α (the same four additions in the same order).

### M147. The isotope recipe's Itoh step does not say that a tracer inside Z also goes into metal_tracer_slots, or it is counted twice

- **Status:** open (doc). The net review's item. Latent: no species has been added, and it needs `use_itoh_neutrino_loss`.
- **In the original F77?** No. NEUTRINO's mixture had four species (M60). Both lists came with M60's fix, [e1d89c2f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e1d89c2f), and the recipe's sentence with [90d39ba2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/90d39ba2) (both 2026-10-29, round 2).
- **Now:** `itoh_slots` with its nucleon numbers and charges, [nuclear_energy.f90:76-91](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L76-L91); `metal_tracer_slots`, "the tracers carried inside Z (composition_layout)", [:92-94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L92-L94); the mixture, each `itoh_slots` species at its slot and then max(0, Z − Σ `metal_tracer_slots`) as Ne20, [:362-365](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L362-L365); `azbar`, [thermal_neutrinos.f90:53-82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/thermal_neutrinos.f90#L53-L82); the layout's statement of the tracers, [composition_layout.f90:10-13](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/composition_layout.f90#L10-L13); the recipe, [net/README.md:191](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/README.md#L191).
- **What is wrong:** step 2 of "Add an isotope" ends: "`nuclear_energy`'s `itoh_slots` (and its nucleon numbers and charges) if it should count in the thermal neutrinos' mean A and Z on its own rather than as part of Z". For a species carried inside Z (Ne20, the recipe's example, would be) that is half the change: unless it also goes into `metal_tracer_slots`, its mass is counted at its slot and again in the Z remainder, so `azbar`'s Σ X/A (Ā = 1/Σ X/A) gains X/A of the tracer: Ā comes out low and Z̄ is shifted towards the tracer's charge; put into `metal_tracer_slots` alone, it drops out of the mixture. `metal_tracer_slots` is a hand copy of composition_layout's "slots 5..11 and 13..15", which nothing ties to the layout, and M90's proposed fix (the metals no screening slot holds, as Ne20) would need the same set a second time.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** which slots are tracers inside Z is said once, and every Z remainder follows it; a recipe names every list a step must touch.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: a named set of the tracer slots in `composition_layout`, used for the Itoh remainder (and by M90's fix); the recipe's step 2 names it. Byte-identical (the same ten slots).

### M148. The source recipe has a new lookup take its mean weights from mean_weights_from_density on a fresh record, which gives NaN R/μ and 1/μ_ion = 0

- **Status:** fixed (doc) in [72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos). The eos review's item, confirmed on a scratch copy of eos_mixture; it extends M123. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The recipe came with [9ce8e797](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9ce8e797) (2026-10-29, round 2), `mean_weights_from_density` with [26751395](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/26751395) (2026-10-29, round 2, M65), and the adopt and blend helpers with [2c03cfba](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2c03cfba) (2026-10-29, round 1).
- **Now:** README §7, "Add an EOS source", [README.md:119-131](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L119-L131): step 1's lookup ([:122](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L122)) and step 4's call ([:128](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L128)); `mean_weights_from_density`, [eos_mixture.f90:145-150](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_mixture.f90#L145-L150); `eos_result`'s defaults, [eos_results.f90:28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L28), [:37-38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L37-L38); `adopt_table_result`, [blended_eos.f90:461-476](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L461-L476); OPAL's lookup, which sets T and P itself ([opal_eos.f90:82-83](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L82-L83)) and takes its mean weights from `compute_mean_weights` ([:157-160](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L157-L160)).
- **What is wrong:** step 1 tells a source's lookup to fill "the mean weights (`mean_weights_from_density` gives R/mu and 1/mu_e from the density)", and step 4 to call the lookup "on a fresh record". The helper computes R/μ = βP/(ρT) from r's T and P and keeps r's 1/μ_ion; a fresh `eos_result` holds T = P = 0 and 1/μ_ion = 0, and step 1's list of the fields to fill names neither T nor P and says nothing of where 1/μ_ion comes from. So R/μ = 0/0 and 1/μ_e are NaN (on a scratch copy of the helper, R/μ, 1/μ_e and 1/μ_ion come out NaN, NaN and 0); a lookup that does set T and P gets the right R/μ but 1/μ_ion = 0 and the whole of 1/μ in 1/μ_e. `adopt_table_result` copies the three into the zone's result ([:469-471](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L469-L471)) and `blend_table_result` blends them in. The helper works where it is used now because each caller hands it a copy of r, which holds T, P and the zone's 1/μ_ion (`gas_eos`'s `scv = r`, [:248](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L248), whose lookup even takes P from r, [scv_eos.f90:60-61](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L60-L61); the ramp's r, [:426](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L426)). A step modelled on `opal_step`, which copies its lookup's T and P into r ([:290-291](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L290-L291)), would zero those in the zone's result too.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a recipe a newcomer follows gives a right result; its lookup's contract says what the lookup is given and what it must fill.
- **What we did:** README §6's source recipe, rewritten for the table-source descriptor, says what a lookup is handed and must fill and which fields `adopt_table_result` and `blend_table_result` carry (with M123's), and was re-traced on a throwaway branch with a toy source. Docs only.

### M149. The table-path recipe, followed literally, gives a registry row whose legacy name is declared nowhere; the generators accept it and the build fails

- **Status:** fixed in [e311ee8e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e311ee8e) and [196f6397](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/196f6397) (2026-10-31, round 3), the recipe in [e149a803](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e149a803). No output. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The registry and its generators are 2026's ([ae73704f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ae73704f), 2026-08-22, the first inlist format). Step 2's "`legacy` and `proposed_name` both the new name" came with [0179bd54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0179bd54), and the table-path recipe's "its inlist name `my_table_file` or the code name" with [685f0d70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/685f0d70) (both 2026-10-29).
- **Now:** `io/README.md` §5, "Add a control" step 2 ([README.md:149](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L149)) and "Add a table path" ([:157-162](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L157-L162), step 2 at [:159](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L159)); the claims at [:120](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L120) ("The controls generators themselves stop when the registry and the declarations disagree") and [:48](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L48). In `gen_inlist`: the entry classes ([gen_inlist.py:139-149](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L139-L149)); the type check, which passes over a legacy name it finds no declaration for ([:150-158](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L150-L158)); the declarations, none for a `keep` row and a warning for a `newlocal` one ([:167-178](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L167-L178)); the copies ([:199-211](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L199-L211)); and `reader_defaults`, which gives the undeclared name its canonical twin's default ([:102-104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L102-L104)).
- **What is wrong:** step 2 of "Add a control" says `legacy` and `proposed_name` are both the new name, which works because a new control's inlist name is its code name (the legacy name is then the buffer member itself). The table-path recipe lets the inlist name differ (`my_table_file` for `my_table_path`) and sends the reader back to that step ("Its registry row as for a control"), so the row gets `legacy` = `proposed_name` = `my_table_file`, `canonical` `my_table_path`. On a scratch copy of `src/` at d6a66ffe with the recipe's steps 1-3 (the declaration, that row, the `expand_value` line):
  - `gen_controls_state`, `gen_inlist` and `gen_controls_dump` all exit 0. The row is a `keep` (inlist name = legacy name), so `gen_inlist` declares nothing for it, yet puts `my_table_file` into the `&control` group (`inlist_new_decl.inc`), `legacy_mirror.inc` (`my_table_file = my_table_path`) and `adopt_canonical.inc` (`my_table_path = my_table_file`), and documents it in `control.defaults` with `my_table_path`'s default.
  - `make` stops at `io/legacy_controls.o`: "legacy_mirror.inc:298:7: Error: Symbol 'my_table_file' at (1) has no IMPLICIT type", in a generated file, not at the row.
  - A legacy name declared nowhere is a disagreement between the registry and the declarations, and no generator stops on it; a `newlocal` row with an undeclared legacy name gets a printed WARNING and a `double precision` local, and exit 0 too.
  - The working fill is `legacy` = `my_table_path`, `proposed_name` = `my_table_file` (a `newlocal` row: `gen_inlist` declares `character(len=256) :: my_table_file` from the buffer's declaration); on a second scratch copy the build links. The inlist name equal to the code name also works, as for any new control.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a recipe says what goes in each cell for each case it offers, and a row the code cannot compile stops the generator with the row's name, as the README says it does.
- **What we did:** a table path's row needs no edit of the read: a path control has the registry type `path`, and `expand_paths.inc` is generated from the path rows; every row has a code name, and the generators stop, naming the row and printing which cells to fill (`gen_inlist.py --cells`), when a code name is not a buffer member of the row's type or a legacy name is in neither frozen namelist (the old recipe's fill, `legacy` = the inlist name, now stops `gen_inlist`). `io/README.md` §5 names the cells for each case (an inlist name equal to the code name, or different: `proposed_name` the inlist name, `canonical` the code name, `legacy` `-`), traced on 2026-10-31 with a table path whose inlist name differs from its code name.

### M150. The recipe for a value the run changes leaves out two steps, so the generated-files and contract tests fail after it

- **Status:** fixed in [28049c9c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/28049c9c) (2026-10-31, round 3), and in [ff74305d](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ff74305d) at the merge. Docs only. The links below show the text before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The recipe came with [5ac2f634](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5ac2f634) and its trace note with [9dabfccf](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9dabfccf), the run-copy column of `controls_registry.md` with [d86d5dce](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d86d5dce) (all 2026-10-30, the controls split).
- **Now:** the recipe, [state/README.md:470](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/README.md#L470); the column, written by `gen_inlist.py` ([gen_inlist.py:326](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L326), [:349](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L349)) into [controls_registry.md:12-16](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.md#L12-L16) and its two tables ([:29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.md#L29), [:158](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.md#L158)); `test_generated_files.py`, which runs every generator with `--check` ([test_generated_files.py:16-24](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/test_generated_files.py#L16-L24)); io/README's recipe, which has both steps ([io/README.md:150-151](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L150-L151), [:155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L155)).
- **What is wrong:** after "put the member's name in the control's `run_copy` cell of the registry" the recipe runs only `gen_controls_state.py` (and ends with `gen_star_docs.py`). The registry's Markdown table carries a run-copy column, so `gen_inlist.py --check` fails until `gen_inlist.py` runs; and moving the readers from `s%physics%x` to the member changes their `star reads:` lines, so `check_star_contracts.py` fails until `--fix`. Traced on a scratch copy with an existing control, `tri_delta_logl`, given a run copy that `surface_boundary` changes and that `timestep_limit_hr` and `compute_surface_boundary` read: after the recipe's steps, `gen_controls_state.py --check`, `gen_star_docs.py --check` and `check_boundaries.py` pass, `gen_inlist.py --check` fails ("controls_registry.md is stale: rerun tools/gen_inlist.py") and `check_star_contracts.py` reports both readers; after `gen_inlist.py` and `check_star_contracts.py --fix`, all six generators' checks, the contracts and `check_boundaries.py` pass. A new control comes through io/README's recipe, which runs both, so a trace with a new control (the note's dummy) could not show the gap.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a traced recipe leaves the tests passing.
- **What we did:** state/README §7's "Add a value the run changes" is numbered steps that name every generator and fix step (`gen_controls_state.py`, `gen_inlist.py`, `check_star_contracts.py --fix`, `gen_star_docs.py`), traced on a throwaway branch with the existing control `tri_delta_logl` given a run copy, the checks run after each step; a new recipe covers a value set per Monte Carlo run. The controls package's dump of every run copy (58f6648f) added a step after that trace, `gen_controls_dump.py` and the dumps' regeneration, which the merge added (ff74305d).

### M151. The Monte Carlo sample that sets the metal settling factor is named and described as a helium parameter

- **Status:** fixed in [7a06885f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7a06885f) (2026-10-31, round 3). Byte-identical; the Monte Carlo summary keeps its format. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. MAIN reads the sixth value of each run's record into `FHE`, copies it to `FZDIF`, and sets the metals' settling factor `FGRZ` from it; `FGRSET`, which it also sets, is a local nothing reads, and the helium factor `FGRY` keeps PARMIN's value. The block's own comment calls the samples "monte carlo parameters for metal diffusion" ([main.f:136-139](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L136-L139), [:217-222](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L217-L222), [:235-236](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L235-L236); SETUP_GRSETT's helium and metal coefficients take `FGRY` and `FGRZ`, [setup_grsett.f:159](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setup_grsett.f#L159), [:250](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setup_grsett.f#L250)):
  ```fortran
  C added monte carlo parameters for metal diffusion, solar L, solar age.
              FZDIF(I) = FHE(I)
           FGRSET = FHE(NN)
           FGRZ = FZDIF(NN)
  ```
  The name `helium_fraction_param`, after the F77's `FHE`, came with [c428adc3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c428adc3) (2026-08-19; its comment: "Naming is local to this batch"), the comment "the helium (diffusion) parameter" with [745af296](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/745af296) (2026-10-29, round 2), and [d86d5dce](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d86d5dce) (2026-10-30, the controls split) carried both into the new `mc_samples` record, one comment per member.
- **Now:** the record, [star_info_lib.f90:126-145](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L126-L145), with `helium_fraction_param` ("the helium (diffusion) parameter") and its copy `diffusion_factor` at [:137-140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L137-L140); `setup_monte_carlo_runs`, which reads the column into `helium_fraction_param` and copies it ([monte_carlo.f90:49-58](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L49-L58)); `apply_monte_carlo_parameters`, whose comment says it right ("sets the metal diffusion factor fgrz only; the helium factor fgry keeps its control value") and which sets `settling_z_factor_in_use` from it ([:104-109](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L104-L109)); `diffusion_settings_from_star`, which puts that member into `fgrz` and `physics%settling_y_factor` into `fgry` ([microphysics_settings.f90:252-253](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/setup/microphysics_settings.f90#L252-L253)); the summary's record 1, which writes both copies ([monte_carlo.f90:204-209](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L204-L209)), as WRTMONTE wrote `FHE` and `FZDIF` ([wrtmonte.f:34-35](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmonte.f#L34-L35)).
- **What is wrong:** the sample file's columns are described only in code comments: no README, registry row or deck comment gives them (the `dynamics_file` row says only how the file is opened), and the file is not checked (M115). monte_carlo's comments call the sixth value "the diffusion factor" and say it sets `fgrz`; the record's comment calls it "the helium (diffusion) parameter", and the name says a helium fraction. The value is a factor on the metals' settling coefficients, and helium's factor never changes under Monte Carlo. A user who reads the record to fill the column, and samples helium settling there, varies the metals' instead, or nothing in a run without metal settling. The shipped sample ([mc_input.dat:1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/examples/run_config_matrix/mc_input.dat#L1), `cm_monte_carlo`) has 1.0 there and its deck settles nothing, so no shipped run is affected.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a member's name and comment say what it holds (M52's rule, as in M117), the more so where they are the only description of an input file's columns.
- **What we did:** the Monte Carlo runs are a lifetime class of their own in `star_info_lib` (`first_mc_run`, `last_mc_run`, `settling_z_factor_in_use`, `mc_samples`), and the sample fields say what they hold: `s11_factor`, `s33_factor`, `s34_factor`, `s17_factor`, `metal_to_h_ratio`, `settling_z_factor` (legacy FHE, the metals' settling factor), `luminosity_factor` and `age_factor`; `diffusion_factor`, the copy FZDIF, is gone, and the summary writes `settling_z_factor` in both of its columns. `gen_star_docs.py` documents and checks the sample fields; four mutations caught.

### M152. The registry describes eight controls by what their run copies do, and five of them are set by no code

- **Status:** fixed in [54b970f8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/54b970f8) and [63628c4a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/63628c4a) (2026-10-31, round 3). Byte-identical; five dump labels dropped, each with one value in all 315 dumps. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The descriptions came with [5f3835a3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5f3835a3) (2026-10-29), when the run changed these values in `star%job` itself (`begin_kind_card` set `s%job%initial_envelope_x` from `initial_x_array` and `s%job%requested_envelope_mass` from `senv0_array`; `step_driver` and `henyey_iteration` ramped `s%job%solver_underrelax_factor`). The controls split ([d86d5dce](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d86d5dce), 2026-10-30) gave each a run copy, a star member, and left the descriptions.
- **Now:** the rows [controls_registry.tsv:2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L2), [:389](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L389), [:391-394](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L391-L394), [:396-397](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L396-L397), copied into `control.defaults` (`mixing_length_alpha`'s) and `controls_registry.md`; the status's description, [controls_registry.py:23-25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L23-L25), and the preamble of the generated table "Members no deck sets", [gen_inlist.py:339-341](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/gen_inlist.py#L339-L341); the five members, [controls_buffer.f90:203](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L203), [:267-273](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L267-L273), [:296-298](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L296-L298); their only reader, `arm_run_copies` ([controls_sync.f90:833-846](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_sync.f90#L833-L846)); the copies set again at each card start and step ([run_driver.f90:344-351](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L344-L351), [step_driver.f90:426](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L426)); ROADMAP's open note ([ROADMAP.md:3282-3283](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/docs/ROADMAP.md#L3282-L3283)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - Since the split the controls never change after the read, yet eight descriptions say what the run does to their copies: `mixing_length_array` "(the solar calibration rewrites the later runs' entries)", `end_age_stop_active` "rewritten by the calibration", `rescale_params` "the calibration rewrites them", `solver_underrelax_factor` "the run ramps it from fcorr0 and fcorri", `requested_envelope_mass` and `change_envelope_mass_flag` "from senv0_array" and "from has_senv0_array at the card start", `initial_envelope_x` and `initial_envelope_z` "from initial_x_array" and "from initial_z_array; a rescale changes it". The status `derived` is a member "that the run keeps (the Newton factor fcorr)", and the table's preamble says "The read computes them (unit numbers, flags derived from other controls) or the run keeps them"; none of the 15 derived rows is a unit number, and the run keeps none of them.
  - Five are set by no code (every assignment searched): `solver_underrelax_factor`, `requested_envelope_mass` and `change_envelope_mass_flag` have no initializer and stay 0, 0 and .false.; `initial_envelope_x` and `initial_envelope_z` stay at their initializers 0.7 and 0.02, not "from initial_x_array". Only `arm_run_copies` reads them (their `used` is `run`), to arm `newton_correction_factor`, `requested_log_fit_point_mass_fraction`, `fit_point_move_requested`, `current_card_envelope_x` and `_z`, which the card start and the step set again. controls_buffer's own comments say the requested envelope mass is "set from the starting model" (:268) and the envelope composition "used by the reader" (:296); neither is.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a control's description says what the deck's value means; what the run does with it belongs to the run copy's comment, which `star_info_lib` and `state/README.md` give for each.
- **What we did:** each control's description is now the comment above its declaration in `io/controls_buffer.f90` (the registry's description column moved there: one source), and the eight say what the control holds and name its run copy; the five members no code set (`solver_underrelax_factor`, `requested_envelope_mass`, `change_envelope_mass_flag`, `initial_envelope_x` and `initial_envelope_z`) are gone, and their former copies are plain run-state members set at the card start and the step from their real sources (`newton_correction_factor`, `requested_log_fit_point_mass_fraction` and `fit_point_move_requested` start at 0 and `.false.` from the template star, as the arming gave them; `current_card_envelope_x` and `_z` have the initializers 0.7d0 and 0.02d0).

### M153. io/README puts the output in star%control, and calls the legacy pair "the same groups"

- **Status:** fixed in [e149a803](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e149a803) (2026-11-01, round 3): the controls package's text, pasted at the merge into the output package's README. Docs only. The links below show the text before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. PARMIN's two namelists are the legacy decks', FSHORT in CONTROL ([parmin.f:262-268](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L262-L268)):
  ```fortran
  C SPLIT NAMELIST INTO TWO: CONTROL and PHYSICS
        NAMELIST /CONTROL/
       *   FLAST, FFIRST, FFERMI, FDEBUG, FTRACK, FSHORT,
  ```
  The inlist's groups are 2026's: [40fa5fd8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/40fa5fd8) (2026-08-28) moved `log_output_file` (FSHORT) to the inlist's other group and [1d83ddb7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1d83ddb7) taught `upgrade_inlist` to follow such moves; the "same groups" sentence came with [01931c03](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/01931c03) (2026-10-13), which named the inlist groups after the legacy ones, and the records paragraph with [5ac2f634](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5ac2f634) (2026-10-30, the controls split).
- **Now:** [README.md:57](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L57) ("a legacy CONTROL/PHYSICS namelist pair (`.nml1`/`.nml2`), the same groups under the legacy names in two files"); the records paragraph, [:91](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L91) ("`star%control` (the `&control` group: the run cards, the files, the output, the calibrations, the starting model's mixture)"); "Add a control" step 1, [:148](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L148). The legacy CONTROL group, [legacy_controls.f90:275-316](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L275-L316); the registry's rows, [controls_registry.tsv:14](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L14), [:366-388](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L366-L388); the output's reads of both records, [yrec_output.f90:85-86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L85-L86), [:151](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L151), [:190](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L190), [history_output.f90:86-87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/history_output.f90#L86-L87), [profile_output.f90:40](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/profile_output.f90#L40), [:63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/profile_output.f90#L63).
- **What is wrong:**
  - The output's controls are in both records. `star%physics` holds `star_history_name`, `profile_interval`, `profile_data_prefix`, `pulse_format`, `write_profile_flag`, `write_pulse_flag`, `terminal_interval` and `compute_neutrino_fluxes`; `star%control` holds `history_columns_file`, `profile_columns_file`, `pulse_gyre_interval` and `isochrone_output_active`; the run log's `log_output_file` and `report_solver_diagnostics` are `&physics` controls that neither record holds. `yrec_output`, `history_output` and `profile_output` each read both records. Of "the files", `star%control` holds the table paths; the run's own files (`first_model_file`, `last_model_file`, `log_output_file`, `isochrone_file`, `dynamics_file`) are `legacy_controls` variables in neither record (their registry `home` is blank).
  - Seven controls are in the legacy CONTROL namelist but in the inlist's `&physics`: `fshort` (`log_output_file`), `terminal_interval`, `report_solver_diagnostics`, `nu_max_sun`, `delta_nu_sun`, `Teff_sun` and `profile_data_prefix` ([legacy_controls.f90:280](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L280), [:287](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L287), [:292-293](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L292-L293)); none goes the other way (recounted: every row's legacy name against the two legacy groups). A deck writer who takes "the same groups" at its word and writes `log_output_file` in `&control` gets a namelist read error; `upgrade_inlist` places the seven right.
  - Step 1 of "Add a control" says to declare it in controls_buffer "in the group it belongs to"; controls_buffer is laid out by topic, the two groups interleaved (its first section, [controls_buffer.f90:41-94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L41-L94), holds both).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the README says which record holds what, since a reader looks for a control in the record and the group the README names.
- **What we did:** `io/README.md` §3 gives the records as a table (record, what it holds, who reads it: `star%control`, `star%physics`, the run copies, the buffer), with the run's own files and the output's controls in their records, beside the output's own table of its controls; §2's step 1 says that the legacy groups are the inlist's except seven controls the CONTROL namelist holds and the inlist's `&physics`, and names them; "Add a control" step 1 declares a control in its group's section and topic.

### M154. The registry's columns no longer mean what tools/controls_registry.py says: live, legacy, the star% canonical, the frozen namelists, report_solver_diagnostics' use

- **Status:** fixed in [e311ee8e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e311ee8e) and [54b970f8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/54b970f8) (2026-10-31, round 3); `report_solver_diagnostics`' use decided otherwise (below). No output. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. The column descriptions came with [5f3835a3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5f3835a3) and [1cd89324](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1cd89324) (2026-10-29); the last `star%` canonical rows left with [99ab5565](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/99ab5565) (2026-10-29, the solar units made controls); the freeze is [f0c14dd6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f0c14dd6)'s decision (2026-10-11), and the Solberg-Hoiland controls joined the legacy PHYSICS namelist with [73ca7732](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/73ca7732) (2026-10-29).
- **Now:** the column descriptions, [controls_registry.py:11](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L11), [:15-19](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L15-L19), [:28-29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L28-L29), and the check that allows a `star%` canonical, [:87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L87); the eight inlist-only rows, [controls_registry.tsv:366-367](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L366-L367), [:370](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L370), [:384-388](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L384-L388); README step 2, [README.md:149](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/README.md#L149); the canonical homes in [legacy_controls.f90:10-11](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L10-L11), [:26-28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L26-L28) and [controls_reader.f90:177-178](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_reader.f90#L177-L178); the freeze, [legacy_controls.f90:24-25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L24-L25), against [:326](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/legacy_controls.f90#L326); `report_solver_diagnostics`' row, [controls_registry.tsv:383](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L383), its installation in run_log, [controls_reader.f90:52](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_reader.f90#L52), [:68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_reader.f90#L68), and the gate, [run_log.f90:33-49](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/run_log.f90#L33-L49).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `live` is "read by both formats, ..., the legacy decks under legacy", and `legacy` "the name in the legacy CONTROL/PHYSICS decks ('-': none)". Eight live rows are read by the inlist only: `history_columns_file`, `profile_columns_file`, `star_history_name`, `profile_interval`, `pulse_format`, `write_profile_flag`, `write_pulse_flag` and `compute_neutrino_fluxes` (recounted: exactly the live rows whose legacy name is in neither legacy namelist). Their `legacy` cell holds the inlist name, as README step 2 tells a newcomer to fill a new control's, and `controls_registry.md` shows it as their legacy name with the status `live`. A legacy deck that sets one, as the table says it may, stops at the namelist read.
  - `canonical` is documented as "`star%<x>` for a star member", and `rows()` requires such a row to have no `home`, but no row has had one since 99ab5565. `legacy_controls`' header ("into their canonical homes (controls_buffer, the star)", "a controls_buffer variable or a star member") and `adopt_canonical_names`' ("its canonical home (controls_buffer or star)") repeat it; every copy in `adopt_canonical.inc` lands in controls_buffer (the routine's own writes to the star, the cross-section scales, the atmosphere choice as read and `use_ttau_relation`, are not canonical homes).
  - `legacy_controls` says "The legacy namelists are frozen: new controls go only into the new format ..., so nothing is added here" (as README :149 and :164 do), yet `solberg_hoiland_velocity_scale` and `solberg_hoiland_mixing_scale` are in the legacy PHYSICS namelist (:326), the only names added to either legacy group since the decision (the groups compared at f0c14dd6 and d6a66ffe).
  - `report_solver_diagnostics` is `home` `buffer`, `used` `read` ("only during the read"), but the read installs it in run_log (`set_solver_diagnostics`), whose copy the run reads at every `solver_diagnostics()` call (24 calls in 12 files outside run_log.f90). The registry has no column for that copy, and check_boundaries' `used` check sees only the buffer member.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each column means one thing, and its description says what the code does: `gen_inlist`, `check_boundaries`, `upgrade_inlist` and the README's recipes all act on the columns.
- **What we did:** the eight inlist-only rows have `legacy` `-` (status `live`, read by the inlist only); every row has a code name, so the `star%` branch of `canonical` and the "or star" comments are gone; the freeze sentence names the Solberg-Hoiland pair as the one later addition to the legacy groups. `report_solver_diagnostics` stays `used` = `read` with home `buffer`, its description naming the gate the read installs it as (`run_messages`' `solver_diagnostics()`), which the run asks; decided (revisable): no record holds it, so `run` would misstate it.

### M155. model_file_header calls MODEL2's disk-locking age and disk angular velocity disk_temperature and disk_pressure

- **Status:** fixed in [70a47ab9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/70a47ab9) (2026-10-31, round 3), the starting model's comment in [b475f0b6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b475f0b6) (2026-11-01, at the merge). No output. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. GETMODEL2 reads TDISK and PDISK, the age in Gyr until which the surface is disk-locked and the disk's angular velocity in rad/s, as GETW and SOLID use them, with PARMIN's defaults ([getmodel2.f:45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getmodel2.f#L45), [getw.f:106](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getw.f#L106), [solid.f:37](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/solid.f#L37), [parmin.f:376](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L376)):
  ```fortran
       &     LROT,LINSTB,LJDOT0,LDISK,TDISK,PDISK,WMAX                     ! getmodel2.f
        IF(LDISK .AND. SAGE.LE.TDISK)LOCK = .TRUE.                         ! getw.f
           WGUESS = PDISK                                                  ! solid.f
        DATA TDISK,PDISK,LDISK/0.0D0,7.2722D-6,.FALSE./                    ! parmin.f
  ```
  The names came with the readability pass [c428adc3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c428adc3) (2026-08-19), which named COMMON/DISK's TDISK and PDISK `disk_temperature` and `disk_pressure`; the controls have since become `disk_locking_age_gyr` and `disk_omega_rad_s`, but `model_file_header` ([641ce4c4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/641ce4c4), 2026-10-29) kept the readers' names. The triangle comment came with [9337e932](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9337e932) (2026-10-12).
