- **Now:** `model_file_header`, [model_files.f90:52-63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/model_files.f90#L52-L63) (the two fields at [:62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/model_files.f90#L62)); `read_model2`'s flags record, [:526-534](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/model_files.f90#L526-L534); the controls, [controls_buffer.f90:171-172](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L171-L172), and their registry rows, [controls_registry.tsv:250-251](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/defaults/controls_registry.tsv#L250-L251); `test_io`'s checks, [test_io.f90:743](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/test/test_io.f90#L743), [:945-946](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/test/test_io.f90#L945-L946). `read_starting_model`'s header, [starting_model.f90:42-43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L42-L43), against [:278-280](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L278-L280) and `reset_state_after_read`, [:349-354](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L349-L354).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `header%disk_temperature` is TDISK, the disk-locking age in Gyr, and `header%disk_pressure` is PDISK, the disk's angular velocity in rad/s; the default 7.2722e-6 is `disk_omega_rad_s`'s (2π/10 d). The registry's rows for the same two values say so ("UNITS: Gyr", "ANGULAR VELOCITY in rad/s"). No caller reads either field (of the header's 24 fields, `read_starting_model` uses the mixing length, the timestep and the extended-composition flag), so the names mislead a reader of the format, not a run.
  - `read_starting_model`'s header says `triangle_orientation` comes "from the model file"; `reset_state_after_read` sets it to 1 after every read (:351), as STARIN set FTRI = 1 ([starin.f:246-250](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L246-L250)), and the same file says so at :278-280. The readers' `header%triangle_orientation` (model_files.f90:47-51) is documented right, and dropped.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a field is named for what it holds, as the controls it mirrors are; a routine's header says where its outputs come from.
- **What we did:** `model_file_header`'s fields are `disk_locking_age_gyr` and `disk_omega_rad_s` (with `test_io`'s checks), its comment says who uses each field, and MESA's column layout is four named formats; `read_starting_model`'s header says that `triangle_orientation` is set to 1 after every read (`reset_state_after_read`), as STARIN set FTRI = 1 after reading it ([starin.f:247](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L247)), not taken from the file.

### M156. Four statements on which source fills which field: OPAL's Z, where the second derivatives come from, want_derivatives under MHD, and η

- **Status:** fixed (doc) in [620c95c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/620c95c7) and [72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos). The eos review's item, with an addition (η under MHD). The behaviour stays; only what is said of it changes. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Behaviour yes; the statements no. OEQOS06 handed ESAC06 the zone's Z, which ESAC06 replaced by its table's (the check commented out), EQSTAT2's OPAL branches replaced the density, the mean weights and the first derivatives only, and ETA was set by EQRELV alone and not interpolated in the ramp ([oeqos06.f:68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/oeqos06.f#L68), [esac06.f:240-248](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac06.f#L240-L248), [eqstat2.f:136](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L136), [:375-389](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L375-L389)):
  ```fortran
        ZTAB=Z                                                          ! oeqos06.f
          z=zz(1)                                                       ! esac06.f
  c        if (ztab .ne. z) then
        ETA = 0.0D0                                                     ! eqstat2.f
  ```
  The statements came with [5d39f836](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5d39f836) (2026-10-11, `eos_result`'s header) and [9ce8e797](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9ce8e797) (2026-10-29, round 2, the README).
- **Now:** README §2.1 step 4 ([README.md:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L43)) and §3 ([:63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L63)); `eos_result`'s header and fields, [eos_results.f90:18-19](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L18-L19), [:39](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L39), [:45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L45); `adopt_table_result`'s comment, [blended_eos.f90:458-460](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L458-L460).
- **What is wrong:**
  - OPAL is evaluated at its table's one Z with the zone's X: neither the density search nor the interpolation takes Z ([opal_eos.f90:95-100](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L95-L100), [:110-116](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L110-L116); the table's own Z at [:691](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L691)), and the zone's Z enters only the mean weights ([:158-160](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L158-L160)). The README does not say so, though it matters wherever a zone's Z is not the table's: the 186 inlists with diffusion of Z, Z rescales, and the carbon and oxygen of helium burning.
  - "Inside an OPAL or SCV table they are the Yale (Saha) solution's" (README :63; "the Yale/SCV ones" at :43 and in `adopt_table_result`'s comment): SCV gives no second derivatives; below the Saha ramp they are the Saha solution's, above the cutoff (log T 6 up to OPAL's 8.3) the fully ionized gas's ([yale_eos.f90:672-673](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L672-L673)), and across the ramp a blend of the two ([blended_eos.f90:433-443](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L433-L443)). O2 records that they are not OPAL's.
  - `eos_result`'s header says the six second derivatives are set only with `want_derivatives` and otherwise keep their values; the MHD path sets them on every call ([mhd_eos.f90:87-96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L87-L96); `compute_mhd_eos` takes no `want_derivatives`, [eos_lib.f90:74-76](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_lib.f90#L74-L76)), as the README says and the header does not.
  - η is "fully ionized gas; 0 otherwise" ([eos_results.f90:39](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L39)). `radiation_share` sets 0 ([blended_eos.f90:209](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L209)) and only the fully ionized gas sets another value ([yale_eos.f90:701-702](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L701-L702)). The Saha ramp does not blend it ([blended_eos.f90:416-444](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L416-L444)), so across the ramp it is the fully ionized gas's at that gas's density while the density is blended, and at the ramp's foot it drops to 0; inside OPAL it is the fully ionized solve's at the Yale density, not OPAL's; under MHD it is the table's ([mhd_eos.f90:103](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L103)). The 0 is itself a value of η (the onset of degeneracy), not a mark that none was computed. It reaches the profile column `eta` and the history's central degeneracy ([structure_equations.f90:273](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/structure/structure_equations.f90#L273), [observables.f90:193](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/core/diagnostics/observables.f90#L193)).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a reader can tell from the README and the record's header which source gave each field, and so how far to trust it.
- **What we did:** README §2 has a table of which source fills which field on each path, with the Z each uses (OPAL at its table's Z; inside a table the second derivatives the Yale/SCV ones; MHD setting them on every call; η) ([72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0)); `eos_result`'s header says that MHD sets the second derivatives on every call and where η comes from, and points to the table ([620c95c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/620c95c7)). Comments and docs only.

### M157. The README's deck counts and five stale comments, and an MHD header that contradicts the pressure it is passed

- **Status:** open: the MHD pressure question only, the authors' (section 1). The counts and the stale comments were corrected in round 1's eos (2026-11-10: [620c95c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/620c95c7), [72b483a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/72b483a0), [dc8755e1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dc8755e1)). The eos review's items 6 and 7, recounted and measured (below). The links below show the code before the corrections.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. The MHD header is Däppen's, and MEQOS passed MHDPX the total log P as now, while reading variable 20, which MHDST1 calls a space-holder, as log P_gas ([mhdpx.f:6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mhdpx.f#L6), [meqos.f:38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/meqos.f#L38), [:54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/meqos.f#L54), [mhdst1.f:98](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mhdst1.f#L98)):
  ```fortran
  C     INPUT   PGL = LOG10 (GAS PRESSURE [DYN/CM2])                    ! mhdpx.f
        CALL MHDPX(P10,T10,XC,R10)                                      ! meqos.f
        BETA=10.0D0**(VARMHD(20)-VARMHD(2))
  C     SPACE-HOLDER VARIABLE (LIKE VAR(20))                            ! mhdst1.f
  ```
  The rest is 2026: the counts came with [9ce8e797](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9ce8e797) (2026-10-29, round 2); the caller named at yale_eos.f90:184 with [cd3b96ad](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/cd3b96ad) (2026-10-29, round 1); the module named at yale_eos_tables.f90:32-33 with [8bcfb584](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8bcfb584), left behind when [64500ba9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/64500ba9) moved the routine (both 2026-10-29, round 2); the 48 MB with [b431c34e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b431c34e) (2026-09-04); the MHD messages' destination with [43e9b717](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/43e9b717) and [d598f70f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d598f70f) (2026-10-29, round 1), before M73's fix [8ea4f7d2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8ea4f7d2) (2026-10-29, round 2) sent `eos_report` to the terminal too.
- **Now:** [README.md:45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L45), [:111](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/README.md#L111); [yale_eos.f90:184](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L184); [yale_eos_tables.f90:32-33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/yale_eos_tables.f90#L32-L33); [opal_eos_tables.f90:344-346](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/opal_eos_tables.f90#L344-L346); [mhd_eos.f90:45-46](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L45-L46), [:126-127](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L126-L127), [:159-160](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L159-L160), [:510](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L510); [mhd_eos_tables.f90:44-52](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd_eos_tables.f90#L44-L52), [:64](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd_eos_tables.f90#L64).
- **What is wrong:**
  - README :45 and :111, "298 of the 304 shipped decks": testsuite/ and examples/ hold 310 decks (`git ls-files`, `*.inlist`), as they did when the lines were written. 304 use OPAL 2006, SCV and the Debye-Hückel correction, 2 SCV and the correction, 4 the Yale EOS with the correction; the count leaves out `examples/class_exercises`' six decks, which use OPAL 2006 and SCV. It is "304 of the 310".
  - yale_eos.f90:184, `compute_saha_eos` "Called from blend_eos.f90": no such file has existed; the caller is `gas_eos` in blended_eos.f90 ([:245-246](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L245-L246)).
  - yale_eos_tables.f90:32-33, "eos_lib's debye_huckel_composition_of": it is eos_mixture's ([eos_mixture.f90:165-213](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_mixture.f90#L165-L213)).
  - opal_eos_tables.f90:344-346, the vintage instances "(48 MB apiece)": `storage_size` on a scratch build of the module gives 15.5 MB for each 2001/2006 instance and 2.0 MB for OPAL 1995's.
  - mhd_eos.f90:45-46, :126-127 and :159-160: their errors come "with a message in the run log"; they are `eos_report` messages, which go to the terminal and the run log ([eos_messages.f90:32-36](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/eos_messages.f90#L32-L36)).
  - mhd_eos.f90:510 (open question): `mhdpx`'s input is "PGL = log10 (gas pressure [dyn/cm2])", but `compute_mhd_eos` passes the total log P ([:70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L70)), the interpolation runs in the tables' column 2 ([:786](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L786), [:792](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L792), [:812](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L812)), β = 10^(slot 20 − slot 2) ([:97](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L97)), and the slot list calls column 2 "log10 total pressure" and 20 "log10 gas pressure", meanings it says it infers from that use. The repository cannot settle it: the tables are not shipped and their documentation is not here, and the code's own check of R/μ ([:104-117](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L104-L117)) agrees under either reading, since the interpolated slot 2 is the log P it was given. The F77's use fits tables that carry the total pressure in column 2 and the gas pressure in Däppen's spare slot 20; then the header, Däppen's, is the stale part (written, presumably, for tables whose column 2 held no radiation). If column 2 is the gas pressure instead, the MHD density ignores radiation pressure, and results would change for an MHD run. No shipped deck sets `use_mhd_eos`, and `test_eos`'s synthetic tables set slot 20 to slot 2 ([test_eos.f90:747](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L747)), so nothing checks it. With the real tables, 10^(slot 2) − 10^(slot 20) = aT⁴/3 at a node would settle it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** counts and comments are true where a reader meets them.
- **What we did:** README §5 gives 304 of the 310 decks (72b483a0); `compute_saha_eos`' caller is `gas_eos` in blended_eos.f90, `debye_huckel_composition_of` is eos_mixture's, and the MHD errors' messages go to the terminal and the run log (620c95c7); the 48 MB went with OPAL 1995's move onto the shared code (dc8755e1, whose message gives 15.5 MB for each 2001/2006 instance); `mhdpx`'s header notes that it is passed the total pressure while Däppen's header says the gas pressure (620c95c7). Open: what column 2 holds, which a table settles as above (with the check in `test_eos`'s MHD path when `YREC_MHD_TABLES` is set), and then the header's word, or P_gas passed.

### M158. numerics_status's comments leave out cspline's cases, and the bad-input text does not name a table out of order

- **Status:** open (doc). The numerics review's item, corrected (below). Messages only, and none yet: no caller passes cspline's `ierr` (M99).
- **In the original F77?** No. `numerics_status` came with [33f6ca61](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/33f6ca61) (2026-10-29, round 1); cspline's codes came with [75a98edc](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/75a98edc) (2026-10-29, round 2), which updated the README's list but not these comments or the text.
- **Now:** the codes' comments, [numerics_status.f90:18-24](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/numerics_status.f90#L18-L24), and the text, [:52-53](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/numerics_status.f90#L52-L53); cspline's cases, [cubic_spline.f90:38-40](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L38-L40), [:52-65](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L52-L65); the README's list, which has them, [numerics/README.md:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/README.md#L43).
- **What is wrong:** the comment on `numerics_coincident_points` lists splint's, polint's, lir's and osplin's cases and not cspline's two equal neighbours; the one on `numerics_bad_input` lists bsstep's and lir's sizes, too few points (osplin, lir) and a NaN pivot, and not cspline's n < 2 or abscissae out of order. The text is "bad input (a size or limit out of range, too few points, or NaN)", so the message for cspline's zigzag table names three causes, none of which applies. Correction to the review: the text is pinned in `test_rotation_kernels`' output ([expected_test_rotation_kernels.out:60](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/rotation/test/expected_test_rotation_kernels.out#L60), osplin's message), not in `test_numerics`'; and the misreport shows only once M99's fix makes the callers report cspline's status.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the status module's comments are where a caller looks up what a code means for a routine, and the text is what the user reads.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: cspline in both comments, and "abscissae out of order" in the text, with the rotation kernels' pin regenerated. Messages and comments only.

### M159. hunt's header gives the increasing table's ends for both directions, and quadratic_spline's header names the type as the function

- **Status:** open (doc). The numerics review's item, confirmed on a scratch copy; it extends M103 (the same header's sentence on a NaN). Comments only.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. Numerical Recipes' HUNT already said that 0 or N means out of range, in either direction ([condopacp.f:186-188](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacp.f#L186-L188)):
  ```fortran
  *     XX must be monotonic, either increasing or decreasing.
  *     JLO=0 or JLO=N is returned to indicate that X is out of range.
  *     JLO on input is taken as the initial guess for JLO on output.
  ```
  The present sentence came with [4a814b28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4a814b28) and quadratic_spline's header with [6721d0b3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6721d0b3) (both 2026-10-29, round 2).
- **Now:** `hunt`'s header, [table_interpolation.f90:362-371](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L362-L371) (the ends at [:369-371](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L369-L371)); the check, which encodes the decreasing case, [test_numerics.f90:1036-1043](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/test/test_numerics.f90#L1036-L1043); `quadratic_spline`'s header, [quadratic_spline.f90:7-11](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L7-L11), the type `interval_arcs` at [:37](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L37) and the function `interval_arcs_of` at [:410](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L410).
- **What is wrong:** "Outside the table it returns 0 (before the first point) or n (at or beyond the last)" is the increasing table's rule. On a decreasing one, x = table(1), on the table, gives 0, and x = table(n) gives n − 1 (scratch copy, table (4, 3, 2, 1): 0 at 4, 3 at 1; n only below 1), as the header's own decreasing convention table(index) > x ≥ table(index+1) implies and the check expects. quadratic_spline's header says "interval_arcs gives an interval's arcs"; that is the type, the function is `interval_arcs_of` (`numerics/README.md` §1 has it right).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a header states the function's conventions for every table it accepts.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: hunt's header gives the decreasing case's ends (0 for x at or above table(1), n − 1 at table(n), n below it), with M103's NaN sentence; quadratic_spline's header names `interval_arcs_of`. Comments only.

### M160. HOW_YREC_WORKS's numerics table has no polint and lists the private search

- **Status:** open (doc). The numerics review's item, its table half (below). Documentation only.
- **In the original F77?** No. The table came with [b73efaf4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b73efaf4) (2026-10-10), when `polint` was already public and `search` private; `numerics/README.md`'s step 4, which tells an author to keep it, with [2cd53247](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2cd53247) (2026-10-29, round 2).
- **Now:** the table, [HOW_YREC_WORKS.md:536-551](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/docs/HOW_YREC_WORKS.md#L536-L551), the searches' row at [:549](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/docs/HOW_YREC_WORKS.md#L549); step 4, [numerics/README.md:98](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/README.md#L98); polint public, [numerics_lib.f90:47](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/numerics_lib.f90#L47), and its callers, [allard_atmosphere.f90:254](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/atm/tables/allard_atmosphere.f90#L254) (six calls) and [rotating_shape.f90:126](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/rotation/shape/rotating_shape.f90#L126); `search`, osplin's private bisection, [quadratic_spline.f90:27-28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L27-L28), [:371-402](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/numerics/quadratic_spline.f90#L371-L402).
- **What is wrong:** the table of "the numerics toolbox (`numerics/`, through `numerics_lib`)" has a row for every public method but `polint` (Neville's algorithm, used by the Allard atmosphere tables and by the shape factors' extrapolation to zero step), and its searches' row lists `search` beside `hunt`, `locate` and `findex`, though `search` is private to `quadratic_spline` and `use numerics_lib, only: search` does not compile.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the table that README step 4 tells authors to maintain lists the public routines, so a newcomer looking for a method finds it there and can use what it lists.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: a polint row (Neville; the Allard tables and the shape factors), and `search` out of the searches' row (or named there as osplin's internal search). Docs only.

### M161. Three net headers and state/README still put the reaction slots in net_configuration

- **Status:** fixed (doc) in [a43d1efa](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a43d1efa) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's star package). The net review's item, corrected (below: when each line went stale). The links below show the text before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. network.f90:21 and :65 came with [77dfc919](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/77dfc919) (round 1), which put the reaction layout in `net_configuration`, and reaction_rates.f90:24-25 with [a1cf682b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a1cf682b) (round 1). [ec2eaaf6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ec2eaaf6) (round 2) moved the slots to `state/reaction_layout`, `net_configuration` re-exporting them, and wrote reaction_layout's header and state/README's row, both true then; [2094bf02](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2094bf02) (round 2, the same evening) made net/'s modules take the slots from `reaction_layout` and left `net_configuration` exporting only its own names, and [9cef61be](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9cef61be) (round 2) moved `map_user_inputs` to io/ (all 2026-10-29).
- **Now:** [network.f90:19-22](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L19-L22) and the module's own recipe, [:64-66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/network.f90#L64-L66); [reaction_rates.f90:23-25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L23-L25), against its own `use reaction_layout` ([:31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L31)); [reaction_layout.f90:4-10](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/reaction_layout.f90#L4-L10); [state/README.md:10](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/state/README.md#L10); `net_configuration`, private, whose own header says the slots are reaction_layout's ([net_configuration.f90:11-19](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/net/net_configuration.f90#L11-L19)); `map_user_inputs`, [io/user_inputs.f90:99](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d6a66ffe/src/io/user_inputs.f90#L99).
- **What is wrong:**

  - reaction_rates.f90:24-25: "the reaction slots and the settings it reads are net_configuration's"; the settings are, the slots are reaction_layout's.
  - reaction_layout.f90:5 ("net_configuration re-exports them to its modules") and state/README.md:10 ("net/'s `net_configuration` re-exports them"): `net_configuration` is `private` and makes public only `net_settings_t`, `net_settings`, `store_net_settings` and `cross_section_scales_from_sstandard`, as its header and net/README §1.1 say.
  - reaction_layout.f90:9: "setup's map_user_inputs"; it is io's.
  - The review dated all of them before ec2eaaf6; reaction_layout's lines and state/README's row were written by it, and went stale with 2094bf02 and 9cef61be. A newcomer who follows network's header rather than net/README §5 looks for the slot in the wrong file.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** comments describe the code as it is now (code style 5).
- **What we did:** network.f90's two places, reaction_rates.f90's header, reaction_layout.f90's header and state/README's row now put the slots in `state/reaction_layout` (net/'s modules use them directly; `net_lib` re-exports them to the star layer), and reaction_layout's header names io's `map_user_inputs` and the star's run copies of the two scales. Comments and docs only; byte-identical.

Read by script from the contracts of the ten builders, these are the only members missing. The table row at :23 mentions "the star's cross-section scales"; the sentence that claims to list the members does not.
