## 11. Found in round 3 (2026-10-31/11-01)

Round 3 took io and state (with setup) toward 9/10 after the fourth evaluation, in three work packages (the controls read, the output and the run files, the star and its builders; `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Round 3: io and state to 9"), merged onto one branch and verified there. Besides the items of sections 9 and 10 it fixed (their entries say how), the packages found these. M166-M168 were found and fixed in the round, and M169-M173 left open (the cleanup round of 2026-11-01 fixed M169, and in io M171-M173: their entries say how); M174, found at the merge, was fixed after it.

- **How they were checked.** As in section 8, against a snapshot of f01bae96, whose outputs the pins hold: every per-deck output file of the 56-deck set byte-compared, the run logs also against the pins, and the unit tests; each fix within the round was verified with the commit that made it. The open items were read again in the merged code and against the F77 import before their entries were written.
- Current-code links point at [b475f0b6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/b475f0b6/src), the round's last code commit.

### M166. test_controls' second-read check wrote its verdict where the test does not look

- **Status:** fixed in [63628c4a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/63628c4a) (2026-10-31), the round's controls package, which found it by a mutation. Test only.
- **In the original F77?** No; `test_controls` and its second-read check are 2026's ([89b04418](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/89b04418), 2026-10-11, and round 2).
- **Now:** the dump's run-copy verdict, inside `dump_controls`' output ([test_controls.f90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/io/test/test_controls.f90)), which `test_a_second_read_starts_from_the_defaults` in [test_controls.py](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/test_controls.py) reads.
- **What was wrong:** the read-twice check of `test_controls` wrote its "a run copy kept the first run's value" line before the dump's marker, and the Python test looks only after the marker, so the line could never fail it: removing the arming of a run copy that is not dumped passed the test.
- **What we did:** the line is written inside the dump; the same mutation now fails `test_a_second_read_starts_from_the_defaults`.

### M167. A `/*` in a Fortran comment of a generated or included file swallows the code after it under make's -cpp

- **Status:** fixed in [54b970f8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/54b970f8) (2026-10-31) for the controls' descriptions, which the generators now refuse; caught in a scratch build. The star package hit the same trap in a hand-written comment (`state/*_layout.f90`, written out by name in [78262046](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/78262046)).
- **In the original F77?** No. The Makefile builds every `.f90` with `-cpp`, a 2026 build rule; the F77 was not preprocessed.
- **Now:** the description parser the generators share, `_descriptions` in [controls_registry.py:244-246](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L244-L246), and the recipe's warning, `io/README.md` §5, "Add a control" step 1.
- **What was wrong:** gfortran's preprocessor (traditional cpp) reads `/*` as the start of a C comment, also inside a Fortran comment, and drops everything to the next `*/`: a description such as "the `defaults/*.defaults` files", moved into `io/controls_buffer.f90` as a member's comment, removed the declarations after it from the compiled file, and the build failed far from the cause (or, with a later `*/`, could have compiled without them).
- **What we did:** the generators stop on `/*` in a buffer member's description, naming the member; the recipe says so. A hand-written comment elsewhere is not checked (proposed: `check_boundaries` rejects `/*` in any Fortran comment under src/).

### M168. The star tools dropped an if-statement's first star reference and read string literals as code

- **Status:** fixed in [d1d14a6b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d1d14a6b) (2026-10-31), with M116. No output; one contract corrected.
- **In the original F77?** No; `check_star_contracts.py` and `gen_star_docs.py` are 2026's ([758cab27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/758cab27), [8ddbf6db](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8ddbf6db)).
- **Now:** the statement scan of [check_star_contracts.py](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/tools/check_star_contracts.py) and [gen_star_docs.py](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/tools/gen_star_docs.py), and their `--self-test` (`test_boundaries.py::test_star_tools_self_test`).
- **What was wrong:** for `if (s%x) s%y = v` both tools took the star references before `=` minus the first as reads, so the condition's first reference was lost (`evolve_step`'s contract missed `physics%new_triangle_init_flag`); `s%x` inside a string literal counted as a read.
- **What we did:** the condition and the target's subscripts count as reads, and string literals are blanked before the scan; `evolve_step`'s contract gained the read; both tools' self-tests cover the cases (six mutations caught).

### M169. A second Monte Carlo run differs from the first at rounding level, by state outside the run copies

- **Status:** fixed in [7ccd60be](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7ccd60be) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's star package). Found by the star package while measuring M95's fix. Results change for the second and later runs of a multi-run Monte Carlo deck only (no shipped deck makes two runs); measured below. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Probably yes, not run: MAIN calls PARMIN once and loops over the runs ([main.f:206](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L206), [:228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L228)), and every COMMON block and saved local carries from one run to the next, as the modules' state does now.
- **Now:** `begin_monte_carlo_run`, [monte_carlo.f90:80-111](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L80-L111), which re-arms every run copy (M95's fix) and nothing else.
- **What is wrong:** with two identical samples (a copy of `cm_monte_carlo` running card 2 to 400 models, with a central D stop), run 2's first model differs from run 1's at about 1e-15 relative (log L 7.9844792214939431e-1 against ...575e-1; log ρ_c and the moments of inertia likewise), and the printed ages of models 50-150 in the ninth digit; the end models agree to the printed digits. Candidates: star members that a card start does not reset and the model read does not overwrite (the envelope triangle's stored state, the rates and first-guess terms), the domains' caches (the EOS and opacity interpolation state), and `evolve_step`'s saved locals (reset only by `yrec_reset`).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each Monte Carlo run is the deck's run again with other samples, so two identical samples give identical runs.
- **What we did:** bisected on a scratch branch with resets switched by environment variables in `begin_monte_carlo_run`: a fresh star per run made the two runs equal, `evolve_step`'s saved locals did not matter, and of the star's members one alone did, `deuterium_burning_rate_start` (the Step snapshot class). `compute_burn_rates` stores the start-of-step deuterium rate only above the burning cutoff, and only while there is deuterium, while `burn_deuterium_region` averages it over a mixed region with the zones beyond the cutoff included, where the end-of-step rate is cleared; run 1 starts with zeros (the template star), run 2 with run 1's last values regridded. `begin_monte_carlo_run` now calls `clear_previous_run_state`, which zeroes that member and clears the settling routines' report flag (`settling_suspended_reported`, so that a run that ended with settling suspended does not make the next log "SETTLING RESUMED"). `test_monte_carlo.py` runs `cm_monte_carlo` with two runs of the same samples and requires equal history rows; it fails with the reset removed.
- **Measured** (binaries before and after, every output byte-compared): run 1 of every deck identical; with identical samples run 2 equals run 1 row for row, where it differed before, on round 3's deck B (170 rows), a two-run solar calibration (1775), a 3 M☉ Kurucz deck (302), a two-run `cm_rot_base` (82) and `cm_monte_carlo` (12). Run 2's drift, before to after: at most |Δlog L| 3.6e-10, 4.5e-10 and 9.2e-10 on round 3's decks A, B and D, 2.8e-8 on the two-run calibration, 2.5e-12 on `cm_monte_carlo`; on the rotating pre-main-sequence deck 0.60 in final log L and a final age of 8.99e5 instead of 1.48e5 yr, because run 2 burned deuterium in its convective envelope at run 1's stale rates. The 56-deck set (single runs) is byte-identical. The same staleness between the cards of one run is M176.

### M170. A missing molecular opacity table ends the run in a Fortran runtime error

- **Status:** fixed in [53164594](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/53164594) (2026-11-10, round 1's kap), with M220; byte-identical. Found by the output package's CI replay, before the table was in the sparse checkout. Error path only. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. READALEX06 opens the table without `IOSTAT` or `STATUS` ([readalex06.f:56](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readalex06.f#L56)):
  ```fortran
        OPEN(UNIT=IALEX06,FILE=FALEX06)
  ```
  L5's fix ([a9de5f99](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a9de5f99)) gave the I/O code's opens `check_io`; kap's table readers kept the F77's opens (M220).
- **Now:** [alex06_opacity.f90:62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/kap/alex06/alex06_opacity.f90#L62).
- **What is wrong:** a missing `alex06_table_path` ends the run in "Fortran runtime error: Cannot open file .../alexmol06gs98.tab" with exit 2, where a reader that follows L5's rule reports and exits 1 (eos's, atm's and kap's conductive table; kap's other readers do not, M220). Without `status='old'`, gfortran opens the path read-write, creating it where the directory allows.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a missing table is reported with its path and stops the run with exit 1, as L5's rule has it.
- **What we did:** with M220: Alexander 2006's open goes through kap's one `open_table` (kap/opacity_table_files.f90: `status='old'`, `action='read'`, `iostat`, `iomsg`), and a missing table returns `ierr` through `kap_init`. Byte-identical.

### M171. The run plan prints "evolve up to****** models" for a card of a million models or more

- **Status:** fixed in [9bbeaf7c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9bbeaf7c) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's io package), with M111. The run logs of the decks with a card of a million models or more change in that line (no pinned log has one). The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, in kind: PARMIN's run plan wrote the count with `I5`, which overflowed above 99999 ([parmin.f:1303-1305](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L1303-L1305)):
  ```fortran
    350          FORMAT(/1X,'RUN #',I3,'   EVOLVE ',I5,
       1         ' MODELS, STARTING',
  ```
  The `i6` came with the run plan's rewrite ([b10d37ff](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b10d37ff), 2026-10-11).
- **Now:** `evolve_from_start_format` and `evolve_from_previous_format`, [run_cards.f90:29-32](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/io/run_cards.f90#L29-L32).
- **What is wrong:** `sample_cases/LowM_HB`'s decks set `max_model_number(2) = 1000000`, which `i6` cannot hold, so the run plan's line reads "evolve up to****** models".
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the run plan states what the run will do.
- **What we did:** the run plan writes its counts through `output_columns`' `integer_field`: an `i6` field when the count fits, so every run plan keeps its layout, and in full after a blank when it does not; the `sample_cases/LowM_HB` decks' line now reads "evolve up to 1000000 models from the previous card's model". The rescale line's relaxation count (`i3`) and the card's line on the terminal (`i6`) are written the same way. `test_io` checks `integer_field`.

### M172. The profile header's initial_z is the current card's Z, 0 on a card whose deck leaves it unset

- **Status:** fixed in [ea47d0c3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ea47d0c3) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's io package). Results change in the profile headers only. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No; the F77 wrote no profile file, and the MESA-format writer came with [eb624a69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/eb624a69) (2026-08-22). The F77's own pulsation model header wrote the card's starting values, `XENV0A(NK)` and `ZENV0A(NK)`, the same way ([wrtmod.f:192-200](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmod.f#L192-L200), [main.f:278-279](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L278-L279)).
- **Now:** `write_profile`'s header, [profile_output.f90:80-86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/io/profile_output.f90#L80-L86), which writes `s%current_card_envelope_z` under `initial_z`.
- **What is wrong:** MESA's profile `initial_z` is the run's initial Z; YREC writes the current card's starting Z, which is 0 on an evolve card whose deck leaves `ZENV0A(k)` unset. `Test_solar_GS_norot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10.nml1` sets `XENV0A(1)` and `ZENV0A(1)` three times (lines 29-30, 38-39 and 46-47), where cards 2 and 3's were meant, so its cards 2-3 write 0. FGONG's globals now take the first card's values (M130's fix), so the two files disagree.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the same quantity under the same name in every file, as MESA writes it.
- **What we did:** the profile header writes `card_initial_z(1)` under `initial_z`, the run's initial Z, as FGONG's glob(4) does; `initial_mass` stays the card's starting mass. Measured before and after with profiles on: `Test_solar_GS_norot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10`'s 8 profiles' `initial_z` 0 to 1.8804e-2 and nothing else; `test_mesa_baselines`' two cases, and the configuration matrix decks tried, identical; no deck of the check sets writes a profile, and history.data is unchanged everywhere. The deck's typo (`XENV0A(1)`/`ZENV0A(1)` three times) stays, a deck fix that changes nothing.

### M173. Writes outside io have no error path

- **Status:** fixed in [8ab987fb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8ab987fb) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's io package), and `log_line`'s own write in [8ac4496c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8ac4496c) (the star package). The physics domains' direct writes to the run log's unit still have no `iostat`, M112's open part (a full disk under them is caught, below). Byte-identical. The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Partly: the F77's writes had no `IOSTAT` either (M138); these are the 2026 writers outside io/ that M138's fix did not reach.
- **Now:** the Monte Carlo summary records, [monte_carlo.f90:256-295](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L256-L295) (`mc_summary_unit`); the neutrino-flux table, [neutrino_flux_output.f90:96-126](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/b475f0b6/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L96-L126); and the run log's own writes, which carry the messages (a failure there cannot be reported in it). The `.mod` and the isochrone file, open for the run, check every write but not the size on disk, so a full disk under gfortran still cuts them silently (M138's fix).
- **What is wrong:** a failed write in these ends the run in a Fortran runtime error (exit 2) or, on a full disk, goes unnoticed, where io's writers report and exit 1.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a failed write is reported like a failed open, exit 1 (L5's and M138's rule).
- **What we did:** the Monte Carlo summary's seven records are written with `iostat` and `iomsg`, each unless an earlier one failed, then checked with `output_files`' `flush_output_file` (the first failed write, or a file shorter on disk), whose ierr `write_monte_carlo_model` returns; `run_files`' `check_run_log` flushes the run log and checks its size on disk after each model's output and at the end (`output_write_model`, `output_close`), so a run whose log fails stops with exit 1; the neutrino-flux table's lines go through `log_line`, which that check covers; and the `.mod` model and each isochrone record end with `flush_output_file` too. gfortran truncates a rewound file at its next write and its inquire-by-unit size follows, so the `.mod` and a run log with `rewind_short_file` are not taken for cut files. `test_io` gained four checks (the `.mod`, the isochrone file and the run log under a file-size limit, and a run log rewound and written shorter); a two-run calibrating Monte Carlo deck and a deck with the neutrino table and the isochrone file on gave identical outputs before and after. Then (8ac4496c) `log_line` and `flush_pending_log` write with `iostat`, a failure left to `check_run_log`, since `log_line` has no ierr to return.

### M174. A run whose history file another run replaced reports a full disk and exits 1

- **Status:** fixed in [fa04ff45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/fa04ff45) (2026-11-01), after the round's merge, and its remaining window in [609c66c3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/609c66c3) (2026-11-03, the sixth-evaluation pass). Error path only: every output of the 56-deck set is byte-identical.
- **In the original F77?** No. The size check came with M138's fix ([ffd5ce50](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ffd5ce50), 2026-10-31); the shared default name, `history.data` in the run log's directory, with the MESA-format output ([eb624a69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/eb624a69), 2026-08-22).
- **Now:** `flush_output_file`, [output_files.f90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/fa04ff45/src/io/output_files.f90), which measures the file the unit has open, through its descriptor, right after the flush; `close_output_file` is that and the close. `write_history_row` ends each row with `flush_output_file`, and `close_history` checks only the close ([history_output.f90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/fa04ff45/src/io/history_output.f90)).
- **What was wrong:** decks that share an output directory write the same `history.data` (the configuration matrix's 20 decks do). gfortran's `status='replace'` opens an existing file with O_TRUNC and keeps it (the same inode), so when two run at once the later run's first row truncates the earlier run's file in place. When that fell after the earlier run's last row, the earlier run's close compared what its unit wrote (`inquire(unit=u, size=)`) with the size at the path after the close (`inquire(file=path, size=)`), found the later run's shorter file, reported "ERROR: cannot write output/history.data: the file on disk is shorter than what was written to it (is the disk full?)" and exited 1, although its own per-deck files were complete. A file renamed or re-created over the path (a new inode) was taken for the run's own the same way. Seen once: `cm_settle_he_z` in check.py's 56-deck run with 8 jobs (exit 1 after its last model); the same deck alone, and the whole set run again, identical to the snapshot. Before the check such runs ended with exit 0 and a history file that is the last starter's.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the check reports a full disk, the case it was made for; a file another process replaced is not this run's write failing.
- **What we did:** first measured, in a scratch program on gfortran 15.2 (a writer, a second process taking the path, and the writer's view): `inquire(unit=, size=)` is the runtime's own count of the bytes it was given, not the open file's size (after another process truncated the file to 190 bytes it still said 130000), and gfortran answers `inquire(file=)` on a file the process has open from the unit as well; the second process's `status='replace'` kept the inode, a removal or a rename gave a new one; gfortran's `fstat` gives the size in a 32-bit integer, wrong past 2 GiB. So `flush_output_file` (new) flushes, then compares the unit's count with the size of the file the unit has open, read through its descriptor (gfortran's `fnum`, and the C library's `lseek` to the end and back to the runtime's offset); on another compiler the size is not measured. Each file is measured right after the flush that hands its bytes over: the files io writes in one go at their close, the history at each row. The history's close checks only the close, since a size check at the run's end would still see another run's in-place truncation after this run's last row as this run's write failing; a full disk under the history is now reported at the row it cuts, not at the run's end. `test_io` gained four checks: a history file that another run truncates in place (the C library's `fopen` with "w", the open `status='replace'` makes) or replaces by a renamed file after this run's last row, and a file io closes whose path another file has taken, close without error; and the size check keeps the unit's place in its file. The first three fail on the code before the fix, with M174's message. The full-disk checks pass (the history's now at its row); six mutations are caught, and one is equivalent (no flush before the measure: gfortran's `inquire` by unit flushes the unit itself). Left at first: a truncation that falls between a flush and its measure (microseconds) would still be reported, and two runs that write one history file at once left it mixed (the later run's head, the earlier run's later rows at their offsets). check.py at 6 jobs then hit the window once: `rv_notrans` stopped at model 500 with M174's message, and was identical run alone (2026-11-02). Fixed in [609c66c3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/609c66c3): `open_output_file` removes the file at the path first, when the run may write it (a read-only file stays, and the open fails as before), so another deck's open makes a new file, and this run keeps writing and measuring its own, now nameless; the path holds the last deck to open it, whole ([output_files.f90:130-154](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/609c66c3/src/io/output_files.f90#L130-L154)). Of the files kept open for the run only the history is shared by shipped decks (18 paths among the 515 decks; no two share a run log, `.mod`, isochrone or Monte Carlo file), so those open as before. `test_io` gained a check that another run's open of a file kept open makes a new one, the first run's checks seeing its own lines ([test_io.f90:1557-1578](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/609c66c3/src/io/test/test_io.f90#L1557-L1578)), and a `history` mode that `test_io.py`'s `test_two_runs_write_one_history_path` runs as two processes on one path, one writing 20000 rows into one open while the other opens the path 4000 times ([test_io.py:104-126](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/609c66c3/test_io.py#L104-L126)): with the open as it was, the first failed with M174's message in five runs of five, and the in-process check failed too; with the fix both runs pass.

## 12. Found in the cleanup round (2026-11-01)

The cleanup round took io and state (with setup) from 8.3 toward 9/10 after the fifth evaluation (`audit/module-evaluation-5-2026-11-01/`), in two packages (`docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Cleanup round: io and state/setup"), merged onto one branch and verified there. The star package found M175-M177: M175 is the evaluation's new finding 1, fixed in the round; M176 came out of M169's bisection and is open; M177 came out of the round's deck runs and was fixed after the merge. The io package found M178-M180 and fixed them in the round: M178 and M179 are the io evaluation's new findings 4 and 5, M180 came from tracing a recipe.

- **How they were checked.** As in section 11: every per-deck output file of the 56-deck set byte-compared against a snapshot, the run logs also against the pins, and the unit tests; M175's fix was measured on nine Monte Carlo and calibrating decks besides, and M177's with two runs that copy their decks to one path at once.
- Current-code links point at [d2fe96ec](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d2fe96ec), the round's last code commit.

### M175. The gray-atmosphere latch outlived the restore of its run copy

- **Status:** fixed in [2765341c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2765341c) (2026-11-01). No output file moves on the decks it reaches; the terminal loses a line.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. MAIN restores KTTAU for each calibration cycle and leaves LTTAU ([main.f:261-262](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L261-L262), [:955-956](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L955-L956)). The Monte Carlo case is 2026's: the F77 carried KTTAU and LTTAU from one run to the next together (PARMIN once), and M95's re-arm (round 3) restored `atm_choice_in_use` alone.
- **What was wrong:** `use_ttau_relation` meant "the run has switched `atm_choice_in_use` to the gray T(τ) relation". `begin_monte_carlo_run` and each solar-calibration cycle restore `atm_choice_in_use` from its control and left the latch set, so a run or cycle that ended on the gray fallback made the next one's first surface boundary print "SWITCH BACK TO KURUCZ/ALLARD ATMOSPHERE", which it never made, and start a new triangle.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a latch says what its run copy did; restoring the copy undoes the switch.
- **What we did:** the member is gone; `surface_boundary`'s `on_gray_fallback(s)` derives it where it is read, `atm_choice_in_use == 0` with `physics%atm_choice /= 0` (the same within a run: every switch to 0 set the latch, the one switch back cleared it). The rule for a latch paired with a run copy is in `state/README.md` §7: derive it from the copy and its control; one that holds more must be reset wherever the copy is re-armed or restored. Measured with binaries before and after: a two-run Monte Carlo deck of a 3 M☉ star with the Kurucz atmosphere, whose run 1 ends on the fallback, loses run 2's false "LOG TEFF OF 3.692 BELOW 3.95 - SWITCH BACK TO KURUCZ" line, with every output file identical (the card's model read asks for a new triangle anyway); round 3's three two-run decks, a two-run calibration, a two-run rotating deck and `Test_solarcal_noGS_norot` with the gray, Kurucz and Allard atmospheres are identical (the fallback never triggers on a solar model); the 56-deck set is identical.

### M176. A card that reads the starting model takes the previous card's start-of-step deuterium rates

- **Status:** open. Found with M169 (2026-11-01). Results change when fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. MIX calls DEUTRATE only while there is deuterium and clears DRATE otherwise, and DEUTRATE stores DRATE0, the start-of-step rate, on the first iteration level only; both are /DEUTER/ COMMON, so a card keeps the last card's DRATE0 where it stores none ([mix.f:168-172](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mix.f#L168-L172), [deutrate.f:55-58](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/deutrate.f#L55-L58)):
  ```fortran
         IF(XH2TEST.GT.1.0D-11)THEN                    ! mix.f
            CALL DEUTRATE(DL,TL,X,XH2,I,ITLVL)
         ELSE
            DRATE(I) = 0.0D0
      IF(ITLVL.EQ.1)THEN                               ! deutrate.f
         DRATE0(I) = DRATE(I)
  ```
- **Now:** `compute_burn_rates`, `core/step/burn_step.f90`, which stores `deuterium_burning_rate_start` above the burning cutoff (`nuclear_logT_cutoffs(1)`) while there is deuterium, and clears `deuterium_burning_rate` beyond it; `burn_deuterium_region`, `net/light_elements.f90`, which mass-averages both over a mixed region.
- **What is wrong:** the zones beyond the cutoff keep their last stored (or regridded) start-of-step rate, so a card that reads the starting model (every solar-calibration cycle after the first, a later card with `first_call_flag`) starts its first burn of a mixed region spanning the cutoff with the previous card's rates there; M169 was the same between Monte Carlo runs. Measured: zeroing them at such a card moves `Test_solarcal_noGS_norot` (ages in the eighth digit; the final model's timestep 1.58557e7 to 1.58558e7 yr; the calibration converges at the same model).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the start-of-step rate beyond the cutoff is zero, as the end-of-step rate is, and a card that starts from the starting model starts as the first card did.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed (the round allowed no results change here). Proposed fix: clear the start rates beyond the cutoff wherever `compute_burn_rates` clears the end rates (with `store_start_rates`), which also makes M169's reset redundant; its own measured commit, since every deck that burns deuterium in a mixed region spanning the cutoff may move.

### M177. A deck whose shared inlist_used another deck rewrote at its start reports a full disk

- **Status:** fixed in [d2fe96ec](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d2fe96ec) (2026-11-01), after the cleanup round's merge. Found by the round's star package in check.py's deck runs with 8 jobs. Error path only: every output of the 56-deck set is byte-identical, and the shared file now always holds one run's whole copy.
- **In the original F77?** No: the copy of the deck (2026) and M138's size check (2026-10-31).
- **Now:** `copy_inlists_used`, [run_files.f90:273-303](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d2fe96ec/src/io/run_files.f90#L273-L303), which writes the copy through `output_files`' `open_replacement_file` and `close_replacement_file` ([output_files.f90:170-222](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d2fe96ec/src/io/output_files.f90#L170-L222)); `write_profile`, `write_fgong_pulse` and `write_gyre_pulse` the same way.
- **What was wrong:** the decks of one directory share `output/inlist_used` and all write it as they start. The copy was written in place (`status='replace'`) and measured after its flush (`flush_output_file`, M174's fix), so when two decks started together one deck's open could truncate the file between the other's writes and its measure (M174's remaining window, hit at every deck's first second rather than at its end): `cm_env_overshoot` and `cm_core_overshoot` each stopped once in 0 s with "ERROR: cannot write output/inlist_used: the file on disk is shorter than what was written to it (is the disk full?)", and were identical to the snapshot when run again alone. A truncation between another run's writes also left a hole of NUL bytes up to that run's offset, so a reader could find a mixed copy. The profiles and pulsation files are written in one go the same way, and share their names when the decks keep the default `profile_data_prefix`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** as M174: the check reports a full disk, not another run's rewrite of a shared file; and the file at the path is one run's whole file.
- **What we did:** a file written in one go (the copy of the deck, a profile, a GYRE or FGONG file) is written under the run's own name, `<path>.<process id>.tmp` in the same directory, flushed, measured and closed there (`close_output_file`, whose messages name the path), then renamed over its path (the C library's `rename`, which replaces the file in one step). A file that fails is removed and the path left as it was; a failed rename is reported. The path always holds one run's whole file, the last to finish, and another run's open never reaches this run's file. The files open for the run (the history, the run log, the `.mod`, the isochrone and Monte Carlo files) keep M174's measure right after each flush; its microsecond window was closed for the history, the one such file decks share, in [609c66c3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/609c66c3) (M174). `test_io.py`'s `test_two_runs_copy_their_decks_to_one_path` starts two `test_io copy` processes at once, each copying its own deck 2000 times to one `output/inlist_used`: both must exit 0, every read of the path while they run and at the end must be one run's whole copy, and nothing else may be left in the directory; the code before the fix failed it in six runs of six, within the first 81 copies, with M177's message. `test_io` gained two checks (a whole copy at its path with no file of the run's own beside it; a copy cut short by a full disk leaves neither). Four mutations caught: the code before the fix, no rename, one temporary name for every run, and no removal of a failed file. Verified after the fix: check.py's 56-deck set at 8 jobs, three times, each with every per-deck file identical to the snapshot (but M171's intended run-plan line), every pin OK and no deck stopped on a shared file; `test_mesa_baselines`, which compares the profiles and pulsation files, passes.

### M178. A deck without run_description wrote NUL bytes into the run log

- **Status:** fixed in [e213c7ef](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e213c7ef) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's io package); the io evaluation's new finding 4. Latent: every shipped deck sets both lines.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. DESCRIP had no value unless the deck set it: it is in COMMON /DESC/, which nothing initializes ([parmin.f:23](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L23), [parmin.f:57](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L57)), so it held zero bytes in practice, and PARMIN wrote both lines into the run log with A80 ([parmin.f:1265-1268](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L1265-L1268)):
  ```fortran
        WRITE(ISHORT,310) DESCRIP(1),  DESCRIP(2)
    310 FORMAT(/,' ',125('='),/,' ',' DESCRIPTION OF RUN: ', A80,/,
  ```
  The 2026 controls buffer declared 256 NUL bytes as the default, while `control.defaults` documented `''`.
- **Now:** `run_description`'s declaration, [controls_buffer.f90:82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d2fe96ec/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L82).
- **What was wrong:** `run_description` defaulted to 256 NUL bytes, and `trim` does not remove NUL, so a deck that left `run_description(2)` unset wrote a run-log line of 14 blanks and 256 NULs (which made `grep` call the log binary), and one that left (1) unset wrote them after "description:".
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a control's default is what its documentation says, and the run log is text.
- **What we did:** a blank default. `test_controls.py`'s `test_a_deck_without_a_description_writes_a_clean_run_log` (a deck that sets neither line writes an empty description, no second line and no NUL byte); a mutation of the generated seed fails it. The controls dumps changed in `pristine.txt`'s two lines only, no hash moved.

### M179. A path expanded past its control's 256 characters, or an output path past 256, was cut silently

- **Status:** fixed in [f36b4e55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f36b4e55) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's io package); the io evaluation's new finding 5. Latent: no shipped path comes near the limit.
- **In the original F77?** No. The F77 took each file name whole from its namelist into a `CHARACTER*256` variable ([parmin.f:21-41](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L21-L41)); the placeholders (`{YREC_INPUT}`, `{YREC_START}`, `{YREC_OUTPUT}`) and the output paths built from the controls are 2026's.
- **Now:** `expand_value(path_value, name, ierr)`, [run_files.f90:314-350](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/d2fe96ec/src/io/run_files.f90#L314-L350); the writers' paths, deferred-length strings (`history_output`, `profile_output`, `yrec_output`'s `interior_gyre_path`).
- **What was wrong:** `expand_value`'s `trim(value) // path_value(n+1:)` cut an expansion that did not fit the 256-character control, and the writers built their output paths in 256-character buffers (320 for the interior GYRE file) the same way, so a long `YREC_INPUT` or output directory (an HPC scratch tree) gave an open error on a cut name, or output written under a wrong name.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a path is used as written, or the run stops and names it.
- **What we did:** `expand_value` reports an expansion that does not fit, naming the control (and an environment variable longer than the 1024 characters it reads), for every path that does not fit, and the read stops before any run log opens (its path may be the one); the output paths are deferred-length strings, never cut. Checks in `test_io` (an expansion that does not fit, one that just fits, a history path from a 300-character directory) and `test_controls`; two mutations caught.

### M180. The pristine controls dump left the run copies at zero, so a new run copy re-pinned every deck

- **Status:** fixed in [bcfdedf1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/bcfdedf1) (2026-11-01, the cleanup round's io package). Test only. Found by tracing io/README's run-copy recipe.
- **In the original F77?** No: `test_controls` and its dumps are 2026's; the hash of each deck's differences from the pristine dump came with the round ([fbb6e382](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/fbb6e382)).
- **Now:** the pristine branch of `test_controls.f90`, which arms the run copies (`arm_run_copies`) before it dumps.
- **What was wrong:** `test_controls` pins each deck's differences from the pristine dump. The pristine dump did not arm the run copies, so they read 0 there and the deck's value in every deck's dump, and a new run copy added a differing line to all 314 hashes and the 20 representative files, where only `pristine.txt` should move: the re-pin hid whatever else changed with it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a new control, or a new run copy, moves `pristine.txt` alone; a deck's hash moves only when what it reads changes.
- **What we did:** the pristine dump arms the run copies from the declared defaults, as a read arms them from the deck's controls; `test_pristine_controls_are_the_defaults` fails without the arming. Traced again: a new control integer with a run copy moved `pristine.txt` by two lines and no hash.

## 13. Found in the sixth evaluation (2026-11-02)

The sixth evaluation (`audit/module-evaluation-6-2026-11-02/`) scored io 8.9, state 8.9 and setup 9.2 of 10, and the pass after it (`docs/ROADMAP.md`) worked in two packages, io (M181-M189) and state/setup (M190-M195). It fixed the findings that change no output, verified as section 12's items: every per-deck output of the 56-deck set byte-identical to a snapshot of 0ef46d4e and every pin unchanged. No commit of the pass changes a result: the three findings whose fix would, M181, M190 and M191, are the authors' to decide, open here with their measured options (section 1, "Decisions needed").

The io package's entries, M181-M189, link the current code at [99d3908d](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/99d3908d), its last code commit before M174's remaining window was fixed (section 11). The state/setup package's entries are M190-M195: M190, M191 and M192 are the state evaluation's new findings 1, 6 and 5, M193 is a "what would raise the score" item for setup, and M194 and M195 are findings 2 and 4; they link the current code at [48604587](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/48604587), the package's last code commit, and the measurements' scripts are in the session's scratchpad (`fix7st/`).

### M181. diffuse_lithium turns on metal settling and five other settling switches, which its description did not say

- **Status:** open: an authors' decision (section 1). Documented since [819c55a9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/819c55a9) (2026-11-02): the descriptions, so `physics.defaults` and `controls_registry.md`, and io/README's `derived_controls` row state every override. Behaviour unchanged.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. PARMIN's two blocks, after the namelists are read ([parmin.f:1130-1144](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L1130-L1144)), and the rotating run's ([parmin.f:912-913](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L912-L913)):
  ```fortran
  C DBG 12/95 ENSURE CORRECT PARAMETERS FOR Z DIFFUSION
   603  IF (LDIFZ) THEN
             LDIFY=.TRUE.
             LTHOUL=.TRUE.
        END IF
  C G SOMERS 04/15; ENSURE CORRECT PARAMETERS FOR LIGHT ELEMENT DIFFUSION.
        IF(LDIFLI)THEN
            LNEWDIF=.TRUE.
            LDIFY=.TRUE.
            LDIFZ=.TRUE.
            LTHOUL=.TRUE.
            LTHOULFIT=.FALSE.
            ILAMBDA=4
        ENDIF
  ```
- **Now:** `derive_diffusion_switches`, [derived_controls.f90:301-314](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/derived_controls.f90#L301-L314), and `derive_rotation_controls`, [:164-166](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/derived_controls.f90#L164-L166) (called at [:95](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/derived_controls.f90#L95)); the descriptions, [controls_buffer.f90:1114-1137](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L1114-L1137), [:1149-1154](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L1149-L1154) and [:889-892](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L889-L892); the routines' choice, [element_diffusion_lib.f90:56](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/element_diffusion/element_diffusion_lib.f90#L56); the triangle's use, [step_driver.f90:416](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L416).
- **What is wrong:** with `diffuse_lithium` on, the read sets `use_diffusion_z`, `diffuse_helium_active`, `use_thoul_diffusion` and `use_new_diffusion_routines` on, `use_thoul_fit` off and `coulomb_log_choice` to 4, whatever the deck sets, and says nothing; the description said only "Include Li/Be in gravitational settling". Counted from what the read gives each of the 515 shipped decks (examples/, testsuite/ and sample_cases/; a scratch build of `test_controls` without the overrides, against the build as it is):
  - 354 decks run with `diffuse_lithium` on, and the override changes one value in them: `use_diffusion_z`, from off to on, in 169 decks (167 inlists: 84 of `run_from_seed_to_start`, 78 of `run_from_start_to_dbl` and the five rotating configuration-matrix decks; and the legacy pairs `Test_solar_GS_norot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10` and `Test_solar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10`). They run with metal settling under a deck line that reads `use_diffusion_z = .FALSE. ! Compute gravitational settling of metals (t/f)` ([cm_rot_base.inlist:96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/examples/run_config_matrix/cm_rot_base.inlist#L96)); `cm_rot_base`'s pinned dump has `physics%use_diffusion_z = T`.
  - The other five overrides change no shipped deck: every deck with `diffuse_lithium` sets them as the read forces them. Three of them are inert there anyway: `use_thoul_diffusion`, `use_thoul_fit` and `coulomb_log_choice` are read only by the original settling routines, and `diffuse_lithium` selects the new ones, the only ones that settle Li and Be.
  - The same pattern, smaller: a rotating run turns on `new_triangle_init_flag`. All 86 rotating shipped decks set it themselves. Its description, "Force a fresh envelope-fit triangle at run start", was also wrong: the flag makes every model's first iteration compute a new triangle (the F77's LNEW0, "REDO ALL 3 ENVELOPES EVERY MODEL"). And `coulomb_log_choice`'s "(4, a constant 2.2, is recommended)", the decks' F77 comment, was inexact: 2 is Noerdlinger's formula, 3 Loeb's, any other value a constant 2.2, and with 4 the full Thoul et al. solution takes each pair of species' own logarithm.
  - M129 counted its reach by deck text (186 inlists with `use_diffusion_z`); by what the decks run with it is 355 (corrected there).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a control does what its description says, and a deck's setting either holds or the run says that it does not. Whether Li/Be settling should bring metal settling with it is the authors' choice: PARMIN has done so since 04/15.
- **What we did:** documented ([819c55a9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/819c55a9)): the descriptions of the nine controls involved state what the read sets, io/README lists the overrides, and the two wrong descriptions are corrected. No message: a `report_note` would move 9 pinned logs. Options for the decision (section 1), each counted on the shipped decks:
  - (a) keep and document (done): moves nothing;
  - (b) `diffuse_lithium` touches only Li and Be: it keeps turning on `use_new_diffusion_routines` and `diffuse_helium_active` (Li/Be settle only in the new routines, and settling runs only with helium settling on) and stops turning on `use_diffusion_z`: the 169 decks' results move (the metals stop settling, and the EOS's and the opacities' two-Z paths turn off), 9 of them pinned (the five rotating configuration-matrix logs, `m0030gs98z018804_prems`, `m0030gs98z018804_Dbl`, the two settling solar pairs), and `test_mesa_baselines`' files of `Test_solar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10`; dropping the other five overrides as well moves no shipped deck;
  - (c) warn (`report_warning`) when the override changes a value: the run logs and terminals of the same 169 decks gain a line, 9 pinned logs move, nothing else.
  The 169 decks could also set `use_diffusion_z = .TRUE.`, so that their text says what they run with; their copies in `output/inlist_used` would move (shipped inlists were not edited in this pass).

### M182. The run log's name was cut at the first `.short` anywhere in its path

- **Status:** fixed in [0a9c34ac](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0a9c34ac) (2026-11-02). Latent: the run log name of every shipped deck (all 515, by what the read gives them) ends in `.short` and has no `.short` elsewhere, which gives the same path as before.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. PARMIN opened the run log at FSHORT as written ([parmin.f:858](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L858)), but cut FSHORT at its first `short` for the acoustic-depth file ([parmin.f:762-763](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L762-L763)):
  ```fortran
  		MRK=INDEX(FSHORT,'short')
  		FCLCD=FSHORT(1:MRK-1)//'calcad'
  ```
  The run log's `.short` to `.log` came with [2b067d75](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2b067d75) (2026-08-22), which took the first occurrence the same way.
- **Now:** `run_log_path`, [run_files.f90:205-224](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/run_files.f90#L205-L224), which `open_run_log` opens ([:185-197](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/run_files.f90#L185-L197)).
- **What was wrong:** `open_run_log` found `.short` with `index(log_output_file, '.short')` and cut the path there ([run_files.f90:186-196](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/io/run_files.f90#L186-L196)): a run log at `runs.short_tests/cm.short` opened `runs.log` in the parent directory, while the output directory, and with it `inlist_used`, the history and the profiles, stayed `runs.short_tests/`; a name `my.shorthand` gave `my.log`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** only the legacy ending is a legacy name; the rest of the path is the user's.
- **What we did:** `run_log_path`, a pure function: a `.log` ending kept, a `.short` ending made `.log`, `.log` added to any other name. Two `test_io` checks (the endings, and `.short` inside a directory or a name); both fail with the old first-occurrence cut.

### M183. GSM files were written in place, not under the run's own name

- **Status:** fixed in [06e9e578](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/06e9e578) (2026-11-02). Only an HDF5 build writes GSM; no shipped deck asks for it.
- **In the original F77?** No: the GSM writer came with [ec77ad33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ec77ad33) (2026-08-23), M177's rename with the cleanup round.
- **Now:** `write_gsm_pulse`, [pulsation_output.f90:163-232](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L163-L232) (the name at [:199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L199), the rename at [:231](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L231)); `finish_replacement_file`, [output_files.f90:213-228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/output_files.f90#L213-L228), which `close_replacement_file` uses too ([:195-205](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/output_files.f90#L195-L205)).
- **What was wrong:** HDF5 created the file at its path (`h5fcreate_f(trim(pulse_path), H5F_ACC_TRUNC_F, ...)`, [pulsation_output.f90:193](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L193)), so decks that keep the default `profile_data_prefix` on an HDF5 build raced on `profile<N>.data.GSM` (M177's class: another run could replace the file or read it half written), and io/README's "the pulsation files ... written under the run's own name" was false for GSM.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** as M177: the path always holds one run's whole file.
- **What we did:** HDF5 creates the file at `replacement_path(pulse_path)`, and `finish_replacement_file` renames it over the path when every call succeeded, or removes it after a failure; `output_files` exports both for a file a library writes itself, and `close_replacement_file` uses the same finish step. GSM still has no size check (HDF5 writes through its own calls), which io/README states. Checked on an exact copy built with `make USE_HDF5=1`: `test_mesa_output`'s GSM test, which now also checks that no file of the run's own is left, passes (h5py reads back the attributes and the 18 datasets), and fails with the rename dropped.

### M184. From profile 10000 on, a profile's GYRE file and an interior GYRE file could share a name

- **Status:** fixed in [9666cf52](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9666cf52) (2026-11-02). Latent: no shipped deck writes interior GYRE files (or profiles); it needs 10,000 profiles with GYRE pulsation files and `pulse_gyre_interval` positive.
- **In the original F77?** No: the interior GYRE file came with [9df62b7e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9df62b7e) (2026-08-20), the profiles' pulsation files with the MESA output (2026-08).
- **Now:** `profile_pulse_path`, [yrec_output.f90:344-362](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L344-L362), with `first_shared_profile` ([:58](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L58)); `interior_gyre_path`, [:255-265](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L255-L265).
- **What was wrong:** the interior GYRE file is `<prefix><model>.data.GYRE`, the model number zero-padded to five digits, and a profile's GYRE file `<prefix><N>.data.GYRE` with N unpadded ([yrec_output.f90:249](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L249), [:305-306](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L305-L306)). From N = 10000 on the two name spaces meet: profile 12345's pulsation file and model 12345's interior file are one path, and the later write replaces the other (with `profile_interval = 1`, both in one `output_write_model`, the interior file last).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** every file a run writes has its own name.
- **What we did:** the profile's pulsation file name is one pure function, `profile_pulse_path`: MESA's `profile<N>.data.<format>`, except that in a run that also writes interior files a profile's GYRE file from profile 10000 on is `profile<N>.data.profile.GYRE`. Decided (revisable): the profile side, so that no file name changes in a run below 10,000 profiles or without interior files; a distinct infix for every interior file would rename every interior file. Two `test_io` checks (MESA's names in each format; from 10000 on a GYRE name no interior file has, across numbers at the digits' edges); three mutations fail them.

### M185. make's first refusal of a bad registry row had no cells guide; a 3-D control broke test_controls' build; a deleted generated file was not remade

- **Status:** fixed in [a3221e06](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a3221e06) and [a7ddf92c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a7ddf92c) (2026-11-02). Tools only.
- **In the original F77?** No: the controls generators and make's rules for them are 2026's.
- **Now:** `homes`, [gen_controls_state.py:67-88](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/tools/gen_controls_state.py#L67-L88); the dump's indices, [gen_controls_dump.py:55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/tools/gen_controls_dump.py#L55), [:69-111](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/tools/gen_controls_dump.py#L69-L111); the stamp rule, [Makefile:100-110](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/Makefile#L100-L110).
- **What was wrong:**
  - make runs `gen_controls_state` first, and its own registry check ([gen_controls_state.py:71-94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/tools/gen_controls_state.py#L71-L94)) was a weaker copy of `controls_registry.check_rows_against_buffer`: it named a misspelled row by its legacy cell ("registry row -: canonical my_scael is not in controls_buffer") and printed no cells guide, so the commonest newcomer slip stopped the build without the guide io/README's "Add a control" step 3 promises;
  - `gen_controls_dump`'s `dump_controls` declared only `i1, i2` ([gen_controls_dump.py:98](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/tools/gen_controls_dump.py#L98)) while its loops index as many dimensions as a member has, so a 3-D control broke `test_controls`' build; its generated header named two files it does not read;
  - the stamp rule's empty recipe for each generated file ([Makefile:104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/Makefile#L104)) took a deleted file as made, and make then failed compiling its user ("Cannot open included file").
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** every refusal make shows carries the cells to fill; a control of any rank dumps; make remakes what it generates.
- **What we did:** `gen_controls_state` runs `check_rows_against_buffer` and prints `CELLS_GUIDE` with the problems (a member without a row and a misspelled row, each through make: the problem named and the guide printed); `dump_controls` declares the indices the largest rank needs (a 3-D control added on the worktree builds and dumps its 12 elements; the file is unchanged for today's controls); the header names its sources; the Makefile removes the stamp when a generated file is missing (four deleted in turn, each remade identical).

### M186. test_controls passed with a stale hashes.txt row or an orphan expected file

- **Status:** fixed in [f673c59f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f673c59f) (2026-11-02). Test only.
- **In the original F77?** No: `test_controls` and its pins are 2026's.
- **Now:** `test_controls_every_deck`, [test_controls.py:100-135](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/test_controls.py#L100-L135).
- **What was wrong:** when `hashes.txt` differed from the computed list, the test failed only for a current deck whose hash moved ([test_controls.py:116-123](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/test_controls.py#L116-L123)): a removed or renamed deck left a row that nothing checks, an expected file could outlive its representative deck, and reordered rows passed.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a pin is either checked or gone.
- **What we did:** a row whose deck is gone fails, naming it; any file of `expected_controls/` that no representative deck writes fails, naming it (a regeneration removes it); a `hashes.txt` that differs with no moved or stale row fails as its order or layout. Three mutations of the pins each fail the new test; the previous test passed all three.

### M187. test_io's run-log checks logged lines they had not filled yet

- **Status:** fixed in [9b226d04](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9b226d04) (2026-11-02). Test only.
- **In the original F77?** No: `test_io` is 2026's.
- **Now:** the fill before the run-log checks, [test_io.f90:1438](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/io/test/test_io.f90#L1438).
- **What was wrong:** "a run log cut short by a full disk" and "rewound and written shorter" logged `deck_lines` before the program filled them, for the copy-of-the-deck checks further down ([test_io.f90:1392-1394](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/io/test/test_io.f90#L1392-L1394), filled at [:1419-1421](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/0ef46d4e/src/io/test/test_io.f90#L1419-L1421)). Under the Makefile's `-finit-local-zero` they were 200 NUL bytes each, which is why the full-disk check exceeded its 2000-byte limit; under ifort or ifx, which the Makefile supports without that flag, they are indeterminate, and blank ones fail the full-disk check spuriously.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a check's input is set before the check.
- **What we did:** the lines are filled before the first check that logs them. With `deck_lines` blanked at the start of the routine, the old order fails the full-disk check and the new one passes.

### M188. The descriptions named other controls by code name, inlist name or alias

- **Status:** fixed in [ba1f6ef5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ba1f6ef5) (2026-11-02). Documents only.
- **In the original F77?** No: the descriptions are 2026's.
- **Now:** `description_problems`, [controls_registry.py:371-431](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L371-L431) (the new rule at [:390-399](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L390-L399) and [:423-426](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/99d3908d/src/tools/controls_registry.py#L423-L426)).
- **What was wrong:** a description named another control by its code name in six places (`use_structure_time_limits` for `lstruct_time`, `mass_accretion_rate` for `mass_change`, `new_species_value` three times for `change_species_value`, and `laol_extrapolation_tolerance` in its own description for `laol_z_tolerance`), by an alias once (`alex95_table_z_list`), and by inlist name everywhere else. `physics.defaults` and `control.defaults` list controls by inlist name, so they pointed readers at names a deck cannot set.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one rule: a description names a control by its inlist name, the name a deck sets.
- **What we did:** the seven descriptions follow the rule, and `description_problems`, which gen_inlist runs (`--check` too), refuses a code name whose inlist name differs, and an alias, naming the inlist name to write. Three mutations (a code name, an alias, a control's own code name) each stop gen_inlist and fail `test_generated_files`.

### M190. A later Monte Carlo run, or a card that re-reads the starting model, takes the previous one's last age as the disk-locking age

- **Status:** open, the authors' decision (section 1). Documented in [dfdff68a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dfdff68a): the member's comment, `clear_previous_run_state`'s, and `state/README.md` §7, which now says the per-run reset holds the members found so far.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. SAGE, the age the disk tests read, is in COMMON /DISK/ ([main.f:85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L85)) and set only after a converged model ([main.f:790-791](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L790-L791), `SAGE = DAGE`); GETW, SECULR and SOLID lock the envelope while `SAGE.LE.TDISK` ([getw.f:106](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getw.f#L106), [seculr.f:81](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/seculr.f#L81), [solid.f:33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/solid.f#L33)), and MDOT ends the accretion at TDISK ([mdot.f:73-84](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mdot.f#L73-L84)). COMMON keeps SAGE from one Monte Carlo run to the next, and no model read sets it.
- **Now:** its one writer, after a converged step ([step_driver.f90:557](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L557)); its readers, among them `omega_from_j`'s convection-zone lock ([omega_profile.f90:185-187](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/rotation/omega_profile.f90#L185-L187)) and `limit_mass_change_timestep` ([mass_change.f90:465-471](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L465-L471)), whose verdict switches the mass change off ([mass_change.f90:130](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L130)); neither `clear_previous_run_state` ([monte_carlo.f90:144-148](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L144-L148)) nor the model read's `reset_state_after_read` ([starting_model.f90:384-395](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L384-L395)) sets it.
- **What is wrong:**
  - The first step of a Monte Carlo run after the first, and of a card with `card_from_starting_model` after an evolved card, reads the previous run's or card's last age: in `omega_from_j` at its first rezone and solve (the convection zone is not held at the disk's Ω when it should be), and in `limit_mass_change_timestep`, where with accretion and disk locking on and that age past `disk_locking_age_gyr` the step becomes dt = (t_disk − age) 10⁹ yr < 0 and the disk is exhausted, so the step goes back in age and `change_mass` switches `mass_change_active` off for the rest of the run.
  - The first step of every run reads 0, the template star's value, not the starting model's age.
  - Reproduced (scratchpad `fix7st/tools/repro_disk_age.py`: `cm_monte_carlo` with accretion of +1e-9 M☉/yr, disk locking with t_disk = 1.59e-4 Gyr, two Monte Carlo runs of identical samples): run 1 accretes until t_disk (M = 1.00000024 → 1.00000066 M☉); run 2's first model is at 1.5797e5 yr, younger than its starting model (1.5834e5 yr), and it never accretes (0.99999963 M☉ throughout).
  - Latent in the shipped decks: none makes two Monte Carlo runs with a finite t_disk or re-reads its starting model after an evolved card, and `test_monte_carlo`'s deck has neither disk locking nor accretion.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each Monte Carlo run is the deck's run again (M95, M169), and a card that starts again from the starting model starts at that model's age; the disk tests read the age of the model being evolved.
- **What we did:** documented it, and measured the options with scratch binaries (not committed):
  - the age set from the model's at every model read (in `reset_state_after_read`): the reproducer's run 2 equals run 1 row for row, and run 1 is unchanged. On the 56-deck set one deck moves, `Test_solarGS98_difrotmixper18p4d0p1`, through run 1's first step: it starts from the birthline model (1.58e-4 Gyr) with t_disk = 1e-4 Gyr, so today that step reads 0 and holds the envelope at the disk's Ω, and under the option it does not (model 2's total J 1.322e50 → 1.286e50; at 4.568 Gyr log L −0.000082 → −0.000026, log Teff 3.761331 → 3.761339, X_c 0.355855 → 0.355795). Of the 539 shipped inlists with disk locking on, no other starts past its t_disk (the 92 Gyrochrones start younger than their 0.01 Gyr);
  - a snapshot of the star at the first `begin_monte_carlo_run`, restored at each later one (the Monte Carlo class excepted): ends the hand list for Monte Carlo runs, not for cards;
  - left as it is.

### M191. Monte Carlo sets cards 2 and 3's stop ages whether or not the solar calibration is on

- **Status:** open, the authors' decision (section 1). Documented in [dfdff68a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dfdff68a) (`apply_monte_carlo_parameters`' comments; `state/README.md` §7's per-Monte-Carlo-run recipe, which had implied the procedure sets only what a run takes from its sample).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: MAIN's Monte Carlo branch sets `ENDAGE(2)=1.0D8` and `ENDAGE(3)=4.57D9`, "input #s should be scaled for a solar age of 4.57 Gyr" ([main.f:241-244](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L241-L244)).
- **Now:** [monte_carlo.f90:208-209](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L208-L209), in `apply_monte_carlo_parameters`; `setup_solar_calibration` sets both again when the calibration is on ([calibration.f90:387-389](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L387-L389)).
- **What is wrong:** the two ages are neither sampled nor scaled by the run's age factor, and they override `target_solar_age` and the deck's `max_age`; only the calibration replaces them. The shipped `cm_monte_carlo` (no calibration) asks `max_age(2) = 4.568D9` and its run plan echoes 4.57E+09 yr, but card 2 runs with 1e8 yr (latent: it stops at its 10 models first).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a deck that does not calibrate stops its cards where it says; the calibration lays out its cycles' ages itself.
- **What we did:** documented it, and measured the options with scratch binaries (not committed). Dropping the two lines, or limiting them to `calibrate_solar_model`: the shipped `cm_monte_carlo`, a two-run copy of it and a two-run solar calibration (3555 history lines) are identical to today in every file under both; `cm_monte_carlo` with card 2 allowed 3000 models stops at 1e8 yr today (model 170) and runs to 4.568e9 yr under both (model 350, the two identical). No shipped deck moves under either.

### M192. check_max_runs passed a run-card control declared with a literal size

- **Status:** fixed in [7ac8009e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7ac8009e) (2026-11-02). Tools only.
- **In the original F77?** No: the check came with the cleanup round ([462120b9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/462120b9), 2026-11-01).
- **Now:** `literal_run_sizes`, called by `check_max_runs` ([check_boundaries.py:792-807](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L792-L807)).
- **What was wrong:** a control counted as per-run only when its buffer dimensions spell `max_runs`, and `controls_registry.type_of` writes `max_runs` as its value before every type comparison. So a new per-run control declared `foo(50)` in `io/controls_buffer.f90`, with a registry cell `real(50)`, passed `check_max_runs`, `check_rows_against_buffer` and its run copy's type check, and would stay at 50 when `max_runs` changes, read out of bounds past card 50.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** `max_runs` (`state/control_slots.f90`) is the one source of the run cards' size; the one hand-written place a size is typed must spell it.
- **What we did:** any buffer member or registry type cell with a dimension equal to `max_runs`' value that is not spelled `max_runs` fails (no other named size is 50; one that ever is would be spelled by its own name, which passes). Confirmed on a scratch copy: a new member `planted_runs(50)`; `rescale_x(50)` with `real(50)`; `rescale_params(4,50)` with `real(4,50)`; a cell `real(50)` alone: each fails, and the two buffer-and-registry cases passed the check before; a member of size 49 passes.

### M193. check_settings_fields counted an array field as set when any one slot was

- **Status:** fixed in [79c54d0b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/79c54d0b) (2026-11-02). Tools only; no builder had left a slot unset.
- **In the original F77?** No: the check came in 2026 ([4f99f42c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4f99f42c), 2026-10-29).
- **Now:** `check_settings_fields` and `unset_slots` ([check_boundaries.py:403-472](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/48604587/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L403-L472)).
- **What was wrong:** a field counted as set when the builder assigned it or any element of it. Rotation's `velocity_scale` and `mixing_scale` are set slot by slot (`i_mech_*`), so a forgotten slot left that mechanism at the type's default with every check passing (`test_rotation_kernels` covers the four present ones).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** every field of a record is set by its builder, the rule the check states (`setup/README.md` §3), slots included.
- **What we did:** an array field is set when assigned whole or at every slot, each subscript a literal or an integer parameter of state/ or a domain, against its declared size; the problem names the slot left unset. With it, `check_settings_lifetimes` (the same commit) checks that a builder is installed as often as the star members it copies change. Confirmed on a scratch copy: a `velocity_scale` or `mixing_scale` slot removed, a slot by a loop variable and `logT_cutoffs` set at slot 1 only each fail (the first passed the check before); a whole-array assignment passes.

### M194. state/README called a star contract a promise of everything the procedure may change

- **Status:** fixed in [b621c57e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b621c57e) (2026-11-02). Docs only.
- **In the original F77?** No: the sentence came with the README's rewrite in round 3 ([78262046](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/78262046), 2026-10-31).
- **Now:** `state/README.md` §3 ("A contract covers the procedure's own body ... not its reach") and `docs/GUIDELINES.md`'s star rule 4.
- **What was wrong:** §3 said the contract "is the stricter promise: it names everything the procedure may change". `check_star_contracts.py` reads the procedure's own body, and a call that passes the star whole carries the callee's contract: `begin_monte_carlo_run` declares `star writes: none` and its callees re-arm every run copy; the evaluation counted 25 such calls from procedures whose contract says `star writes: none`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the docs say what the check checks.
- **What we did:** §3 and rule 4 say the lists cover the body, not the reach, with that example. The optional `star calls:` line the evaluation proposed was not added: it would add a third line to 54 of the 151 star-taking procedures' contracts, 10 of them in io/, the other package's files, and the callees are in the code.
